cases.content: '''Case Opened''' on 18:29, 10 October 2006 (UTC) '''Case Closed''' on 08:07, 3 November 2006 (UTC) Please do not edit this page directly unless you wish to become a participant in this request. (All participants are subject to Arbitration Committee decisions, and the ArbCom will consider each participant's role in the dispute.) Comments are very welcome on the [[Wikipedia talk:{{PAGENAME}}|Talk page]], and will be read, in full. Evidence, no matter who can provide it, is very welcome at [[/Evidence]]. Evidence is more useful than comments. Arbitrators will be working on evidence and suggesting proposed decisions at [[/Workshop]] and voting on proposed decisions at [[/Proposed decision]]. ==Involved parties== * {{Userlinks|GreekWarrior}}. * {{Userlinks|Tony_Sidaway}}. * And others * {{userlinks|NickOfCyprus}} ; Confirmation that all parties are aware of the request ; Confirmation that other steps in [[Wikipedia:dispute resolution|dispute resolution]] have been tried : '''Initiated by ''' GreekWarrior '''at''' --[[User:GreekWarrior|GreekWarrior]] 09:40, 6 October 2006 (UTC) == Statement by {GreekWarrior}== : I am a proud Greek, yes it is true I do not believe the Srebrenica Massacre occurred, and I *do* believe that eventually there will be a final showdown between Greece and Turkey and I will be proud to fight for Greece against them. But this is besides the point, I have made many good articles, Tony Sidaway can show you these, even he knows about them. But..... I am asking that I a) be unbanned or b) have my sentence of indefinate ban commuted to a ban of a set time period. I believe my devotion to Byzantine topics is at least something that should be taken into account. ::'''UPDATE''' Ok, I can understand if you don't believe I will change my ways, to be honest a lot of what I did was to get a rise out of people, some of it was genuine anger, but here is my proposal, the ArbCom gives me a ban of fixed time and then fixes some kind of 'suspended sentence' on me and I will get a Permanent Ban upon ANY infringement in future. There is still a lot of work I need to do in topics relating to Greek Culture. Especially greek dance. == Statement by Tony Sidaway== I was involved in attempts to get GreekWarrior to modify his behavior, and ultimately in negotiating a community-supported long block when these attempts failed. On his recent return and resumption of disruptive editing I supported a further community ban. I have been in communication with him in email in which I said I did not feel that even his high quality contributions outweighed his very inflammatory attacks on muslims, Turks and others, but advised him that he could try appealing to the Arbitration Committee. And here we are. --[[User talk:Tony Sidaway|Tony Sidaway]] 13:37, 6 October 2006 (UTC) : He does show great willingness to contribute so perhaps mentorship might be the way to go. --[[User talk:Tony Sidaway|Tony Sidaway]] 03:09, 8 October 2006 (UTC) == Statement by uninvolved user Future Perfect at Sunrise== Just for the record: GreekWarrior (probably identical with {{user|NickOfCyprus}} and several known IPs) was community indef banned for repeated, blatant ethnic insults and hate speech ([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Minorities_in_Greece&curid=4782735&diff=78031492&oldid=76364171], [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Byzantine_Empire&diff=prev&oldid=77079243], [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Manuel_II_Palaiologos&diff=prev&oldid=76385332]), as well as self-admitted block evasion during an earlier 6-months block ([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Adam_Carr&diff=prev&oldid=77747351]), which had been imposed for the same reasons. Evidence is at [[Wikipedia:Requests for checkuser/Case/GreekWarrior|his RFCU]], an older [[Wikipedia:Administrators' noticeboard/Archive26#User:GreekWarrior|WP:AN]] debate, and the recent [[Wikipedia:Administrators' noticeboard/IncidentArchive138#User_GreekWarrior|WP:ANI]] debate that lead to his latest ban. I can testify that he has made some decent contributions to Byzantine-related topics, but he doesn't seem to show any willingness to change his completely unacceptable behaviour. [[User:Future Perfect at Sunrise|Fut.Perf.]] [[User talk:Future Perfect at Sunrise|☼]] 11:39, 6 October 2006 (UTC) == Comment by [[User:Improv|Improv]]== This user's userpage was once a textbook case (focusing on but not exclusive to Image:Hellenicrepublic1.jpg ) for inflammatory, divisive, and poisonous content, and his statement above illustrates that his combative attitude and urge to fight will continue. I strongly urge the arbitration committee to reject the appeal and let the block stand. Even if he has made some positive contributions, the damage to the community and the project (relating to whom it drives away) far outweighs the good he can do. --[[User:Improv|Improv]] 17:46, 6 October 2006 (UTC) ==Preliminary decisions== === Arbitrators' opinion on hearing this matter (4/0/0/0)=== *Accepted as appeal of indefinite ban [[User:Fred Bauder|Fred Bauder]] 13:53, 6 October 2006 (UTC) *Accept. [[User:Dmcdevit|Dmcdevit]]·[[User talk:Dmcdevit|t]] 16:38, 6 October 2006 (UTC) *Accept. [[User:Charles Matthews|Charles Matthews]] 14:09, 7 October 2006 (UTC) *Accept, [[User:Morven|Matthew Brown (Morven)]] ([[User talk:Morven|T]]:[[Special:Contributions/Morven|C]]) 17:59, 9 October 2006 (UTC) ---- ===Temporary injunction (none)=== =Final decision = ''All numbering based on [[/Proposed decision]]'' (vote counts and comments are there as well) ==Principles== ===Community bans and second chances=== 1) Users who exhaust the community's patience, repeatedly engaging in disruptive behavior, may be banned upon community consensus. However, banned users with prior productive edits who believably repent of their previous behavior and promise to edit constructively may be readmitted under restriction. :''Passed 7 to 0 at 08:06, 3 November 2006 (UTC)'' ==Findings of Fact== ===GreekWarrior banned=== 1) GreekWarrior was banned by the community for severe disruptive behavior, including racist comments, personal attacks, edit warring, block evasion with sockpuppets, vandalism, and general trolling. [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special:Log&type=block&page=User:GreekWarrior] ([[Wikipedia:Requests_for_arbitration/GreekWarrior/Evidence#Evidence_presented_by_Tony_Sidaway|evidence]]) In response, GreekWarrior has brought this arbitration case, acknowledging his mistakes ([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Requests_for_arbitration/GreekWarrior/Evidence&diff=80954146&oldid=80953943 "I was clearly wrong on these occasions"] and [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Future_Perfect_at_Sunrise&diff=prev&oldid=79859369 "I have admitted I was wrong. I will try to change."]) and promising only constructive edits if allowed back. :''Passed 7 to 0 at 08:06, 3 November 2006 (UTC)'' ===GreekWarrior has recently used a disruptive sockpuppet for evasion=== 2) CheckUser confirms that on October 24, after his promises of reform, GreekWarrior registered the account [[User:DigenisAkritas|{{{2|DigenisAkritas}}}]] ([[User talk:DigenisAkritas|talk]]{{·}} [[Special:Contributions/DigenisAkritas|contribs]]) and used it to evade his ban. The account was used, among other things for racist slogans and threatening solicitation of meatpuppetry. :''Passed 7 to 0 at 08:06, 3 November 2006 (UTC)'' ==Remedies== ''Note: All remedies that refer to a period of time, for example to a ban of X months or a revert parole of Y months, are to run concurrently unless otherwise stated.'' ===GreekWarrior banned=== 3) GreekWarrior is banned from editing Wikipedia for one year. :''Passed 7 to 0 at 08:06, 3 November 2006 (UTC)'' ===GreekWarrior placed on probation=== 4) Following any ban GreekWarrior is placed on probation. He may be banned for an appropriate period should he engage in disruptive behavior. :''Passed 6 to 0 at 08:06, 3 November 2006 (UTC)'' ==Enforcement== ===Log of blocks and bans=== 1) All blocks or bans to be logged at [[Wikipedia:Requests_for_arbitration/GreekWarrior#Log_of_blocks_and_bans]]. :''Passed 6 to 0 at 08:06, 3 November 2006 (UTC)'' ==Log of blocks and bans== Log any block, ban or extension under any remedy in this decision here. Minimum information includes name of administrator, date and time, what was done and the basis for doing it. * I have blocked {{userlinks|GreekWarrior}} for 1 year by on 08:09, 3 November 2006 (UTC) according to [[Wikipedia:Requests_for_arbitration/GreekWarrior#GreekWarrior_banned_2]] --[[User:Srikeit|Srik]][[User:Srikeit/Esperanza|e]][[User:Srikeit|it]] ([[User talk:Srikeit|Talk]] | [[Special:Emailuser/Srikeit|Email]]) 08:46, 3 November 2006 (UTC) * IP sockpuppet {{ipvandal|86.138.3.186}} blocked for a month by [[User:Khoikhoi]]. Logged: [[User:Future Perfect at Sunrise|Fut.Perf.]] [[User talk:Future Perfect at Sunrise|☼]] 19:38, 20 November 2006 (UTC) * 21:20, 28 November 2006 [[User:Khoikhoi|Khoikhoi]] blocked {{user|86.141.243.11}} with an expiry time of 1 month (IP recently used by banned user GreekWarrior) * 02:43, 31 December 2006 [[User:Khoikhoi|Khoikhoi]] blocked {{user|86.133.189.131}} with an expiry time of 1 week (IP recently used by banned user GreekWarrior) * 02:47, 31 December 2006 [[User:Khoikhoi|Khoikhoi]] blocked {{user|86.133.188.138}} with an expiry time of 1 week (IP recently used by banned user GreekWarrior) * 19:07, 13 January 2007 [[User:Khoikhoi|Khoikhoi]] blocked {{user|86.143.172.117}} with an expiry time of 1 month (IP recently used by banned user GreekWarrior) * 20:53, 13 January 2007 [[User:Future Perfect at Sunrise|Fut.Perf.]] blocked {{user|Writingthewrongs}} with an expiry time of indefinite (User:GreekWarrior sockpuppet) * 21:47, 15 February 2007 [[User:Khoikhoi|Khoikhoi]] blocked {{user|86.144.84.207}} with an expiry time of 1 month (IP recently used by banned user GreekWarrior) * 21:49, 15 February 2007 [[User:Khoikhoi|Khoikhoi]] blocked {{user|GreekWarrior}} with an expiry time of 1 year (reset due to block evasion as 86.144.84.207) [[Category:Wikipedia arbitration cases|{{SUBPAGENAME}}]] {{NOINDEX}}

cases.content:
<big>'''Case Opened''' on 26 March 2005</big>  

<big>'''Case Closed''' on 18:53, 10 Apr 2005 (UTC)</big>  

Please do not edit this page directly unless you wish to become a participant in this request. (All participants are subject to Arbitration Committee decisions, and the ArbCom will consider each participant's role in the dispute.) Comments are very welcome on the [[Wikipedia talk:{{PAGENAME}}|Talk page]], and will be read, in full. Evidence, no matter who can provide it, is very welcome at [[/Evidence]]. Evidence is more useful than comments. 

Arbitrators will be working on a proposed decision at [[/Proposed decision]]. 

==Involved parties==
<!--provide links to the user page of each party and to all accounts they have edited with. Briefly summarize case. No details. -->

* [[User:GRider|GRider]] 
* [[User:Kierano|Kierano]] 

==Statement by [[User:Kierano|Kierano]]==
Please limit your statement to 500 words

Refer to [[Wikipedia:Requests for comment/GRider2]], [[Wikipedia:Requests for comment/GRider]].

* User GRider has been mass-adding pages to the VfD list, in a manner which the request for comments pages would indicate is not consistent with the Wikipedia-established VfD policy.
* GRider has not replied on the request for comment page, though he has replied on his [[User_talk:GRider#RfC|talk page]], but in a manner which indicates that he does not acknowledge that there is a problem with his behaviour.
* GRider has engaged in [[Wikipedia:Requests_for_comment/GRider2#Further_disruption|further disruption]] of the Wikipedia, most likely to make a point.
*This has not been added to the Mediation List, as it is not a dispute between two users, or between an affiliated group of users. The request for comments page would indicate that a number of unaffiliated users have recognised problems in GRider's behaviour.
--[[User:Kierano|Kieran]] 09:42, 23 Mar 2005 (UTC)

=== The Core Issue ===

I think the core issue here is that [[User:GRider|GRider]] is on a [[User:GRider/Crusades|crusade]] to change the VfD policy, and that he/she is using the VfD process, and other Wikipedia mechanisms, to carry out this crusade, rather than engaging in discussion and attempting to arrive at consensus with the rest of the community. --[[User:Kierano|Kieran]] 10:04, 24 Mar 2005 (UTC)

=== Examples of Disruptive Behaviour ===

*Editing another user's page (including the other user's words) [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User:An%E1rion/VFDabuse&action=history]
*Repeatedly trying to merge/delete an article that had survived the VfD process [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raph_Levien&action=history]
*[[Wikipedia:Featured_article_candidates/Evil_reptilian_kitten-eater_from_another_planet |Putting an article up for featured article]], after [[Wikipedia:Votes_for_deletion/Evil_reptilian_kitten-eater_from_another_planet |failing to have it deleted]]. (Presumably in an attempt to make a point.)
*Nominating an article for VfD that was beyond his realm of expertise, based apparently on a mention in the article's text of its "rarity". [[Scalpelling]]
*Nominating articles for VfD, but marking the edit as minor, and not mentioning the VfD nomination in the edit summary (most of his VfD nominations).
--[[User:Kierano|Kieran]] 10:04, 24 Mar 2005 (UTC)


===Suggested Actions===

Although GRider has not ceased in his behaviour, despite extensive requests by other users that he do so, he appears to be a valid contributer to the Wikipedia, and banning him would most likely be counter-productive. Part of the reason for bringing this to arbitration is that there are numerous cases of GRider ignoring comments by other users, even to the extent of deleting those comments from his discussion page, indicating an unwillingness on his/her part to discuss the issue.

I would suggest that the threat of serious action might be enough to bring the issue to discussion, and hopefully resolution.

--[[User:Kierano|Kieran]] 10:11, 23 Mar 2005 (UTC)

<!--Add additional statements if necessary, for each directly involved user. Comments by users outside the dispute go on the talk page.-->

==Preliminary decisions==
===Arbitrators' opinions on hearing this matter (5/0/0/0)===
*Weak accept; I don't really know if this case is worthy of our attention, but I also don't see another feasible way to deal with the situation. -- [[User:Grunt|Grun]][[User talk:Grunt|t]] [[European Union|🇪🇺]] 19:57, 2005 Mar 23 (UTC)
*Accept, though this case is mild. [[User:Neutrality|Neutrality]]<sup>[[User talk:Neutrality|talk]]</sup> 23:46, Mar 23, 2005 (UTC)
*Accept. Concur with Grunt and Neutrality. [[User:Ambi|Ambi]] 03:35, 24 Mar 2005 (UTC)
*Accept, though I should note I've passed adverse comment on Grider's methods on a couple of VFD votes - [[User:David Gerard|David Gerard]] 10:59, 24 Mar 2005 (UTC)
* Accept [[User:The Epopt|➥the Epopt]] 04:47, 25 Mar 2005 (UTC)
* Accept. [[User:Raul654|→Raul654]] 18:16, Mar 25, 2005 (UTC)

===Temporary injunction===
1) Due to a demonstrated tendency toward disruptive editing habits on deletion-related pages, [[User:GRider|GRider]] is prohibited from editing any [[Template:Deletiontools|deletion-related page]] for the duration of the case. Should he do so, he may be blocked for up to a week by an [[Wikipedia:Administrators|administrator]]. Determining what is "deletion-related" is left to the discretion of the blocking administrator.

:''Passed 7 to 0 at 14:47, 2005 Apr 3 (UTC)''

=Final decision =
''All numbering based on [[/Proposed decision]]'' (vote counts and comments are there as well)
==Principles==

===Don't disrupt Wikipedia to illustrate a point===
1) [[Wikipedia:Don't disrupt Wikipedia to illustrate a point|Don't disrupt Wikipedia to illustrate a point]].

:''Passed 7 to 0 at 18:53, 10 Apr 2005 (UTC)''

===Consensus===
2) As put forward in [[Wikipedia:Dispute resolution]], Wikipedia works by building consensus. This is done through the use of polite discussion, in an attempt to develop a consensus regarding proper application of [[Wikipedia:Policies and guidelines]] such as [[Wikipedia:Neutral point of view]]. [[Wikipedia:Current surveys|Surveys]] and the [[Wikipedia:Requests for comment|Request for comment]] process are designed to assist consensus-building when normal talk page communication has not worked. 

:''Passed 7 to 0 at 18:53, 10 Apr 2005 (UTC)''

==Findings of Fact==

===Frivolous VfD nominations===
1) [[User:GRider|GRider]] has made nominations on [[Wikipedia:Votes for Deletion|Votes for Deletion]] which are widely viewed as frivolous. [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Votes_for_deletion/Google_test&diff=prev&oldid=11034507] ([[Wikipedia:Votes for deletion/Google test|current iteration]]), [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Votes_for_deletion/Bay_of_Eldanna&diff=prev&oldid=11263561] ([[Wikipedia:Votes for deletion/Bay of Eldanna|current iteration]])

:''Passed 7 to 0 at 18:53, 10 Apr 2005 (UTC)''

===Refusal to accept VfD results===
2) [[User:GRider|GRider]] has refused to accept community VfD results. [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Votes_for_deletion/Bellevue_West_High_School&diff=next&oldid=11385520] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bellevue_West_High_School&diff=11404023&oldid=11403248] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bellevue_West_High_School&diff=11440968&oldid=11438202] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bellevue_West_High_School&diff=11456905&oldid=11441105] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bellevue_West_High_School&diff=11519480&oldid=11513934] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bellevue_West_High_School&diff=11520760&oldid=11519819]

:''Passed 7 to 0 at 18:53, 10 Apr 2005 (UTC)''

==Remedies==
''Note: All remedies that refer to a period of time, for example to a ban of X months or a revert parole of Y months, are to run concurrently unless otherwise stated.''

===Deletion restrictions===

1.3) [[User:GRider|GRider]] is prohibited from editing any [[Template:Deletiontools|deletion-related page]] for a period of one year. Should he do so, he may be blocked for up to a week by an [[Wikipedia:Administrators|administrator]] and shall have the parole reset. Determining what is "deletion-related" is left to the discretion of the blocking administrator.

cases.title: Wikipedia:Requests for arbitration/Guanaco, MarkSweep, et al
cases.content: '''Case Opened''' on 16:39, 8 March 2006 (UTC) '''Case Closed''' on 00:16, 12 April 2006 (UTC) '''Case amended''' on 13:45, 27 August 2014 (UTC) Please do not edit this page directly unless you wish to become a participant in this request. (All participants are subject to Arbitration Committee decisions, and the ArbCom will consider each participant's role in the dispute.) Comments are very welcome on the [[Wikipedia talk:{{PAGENAME}}|Talk page]], and will be read, in full. Evidence, no matter who can provide it, is very welcome at [[/Evidence]]. Evidence is more useful than comments. Arbitrators will be working on evidence and suggesting proposed decisions at [[/Workshop]] and voting on proposed decisions at [[/Proposed decision]]. ==Involved parties== * {{admin|Guanaco}} * {{admin|MarkSweep}} * {{admin|Friday}} * {{admin|Evilphoenix}} * {{admin|Zocky}} * {{admin|Kelly_Martin}} ** (who brought this application for arbitration) This case involves a high-profile sterile edit war between two administrators who should know better. ; Confirmation that all parties are aware of the request * Guanaco: [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Guanaco&diff=prev&oldid=42408682] * MarkSweep: [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:MarkSweep&diff=prev&oldid=42408764] * Friday: [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Friday&diff=prev&oldid=42408829] * Evilphoenix: [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Evilphoenix&diff=prev&oldid=42408864] * Zocky: [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Zocky&diff=prev&oldid=42408847] ; Confirmation that other steps in [[Wikipedia:dispute resolution|dispute resolution]] have been tried This RfAr is being filed by a disinterested third party. Given the total lack of communication between the parties in this case to date, and the attitudes exhibited at least by [[User:Guanaco]], it seems unlikely that attempts at resolution less than Arbitration will resolve this matter. Furthermore, the most sensible resolution to this affair involves a desysoping, which only the ArbCom can provide. —''The preceding [[Wikipedia:Sign your posts on talk pages|unsigned]] comment was added by'' [[User:Kelly_Martin|Kelly_Martin]] ([[User talk:Kelly_Martin|talk]] • [[Special:Contributions/Kelly_Martin|contribs]]) {{{2|}}}. ===Requests for comment=== === Statement by Kelly Martin, third party bringing the case=== Starting at about 00:31 on March 2, {{admin|MarkSweep}} removed, without any prior discussion I've been able to find, categories from over 100 userboxes (e.g. [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:User_not-Drug-free&diff=prev&oldid=41828378]). During this same interval he was also substing userboxes into user's pages (e.g. [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User:God_of_War/Userboxen&diff=prev&oldid=41865522]). In some cases, MarkSweep editwarred with other editors over these reversions, eventually getting blocked at 11:32 by {{admin|Zocky}} for a 3RR violation on [[Template:User pro-cannabis]]. At 21:32 {{admin|Guanaco}} reblocked MarkSweep for the same 3RR violation (the previous block having expired), but unblocked him 5 minutes later after discovering that he'd been previously blocked. Guanaco then, starting at about 22:25, used the vandalism rollback tool to revert most of MarkSweep's edits (both removal of categories and substitutions of user pages) (e.g. [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:User_deviantART&diff=prev&oldid=41961971]). Starting at about 03:27 on March 3, 2006, MarkSweep used the vandalism rollback tool to revert most of Guanaco's edits (e.g. [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:User_sxe&diff=prev&oldid=42000120]), again without any discussion I can find. Starting at about 04:20 on March 4, 2006, Guanaco used the vandalism rollback tool to rerevert most of MarkSweep's reverts (e.g. [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:User_freemason&diff=prev&oldid=42153785]) MarkSweep has not communicated with Guanaco in any way during this affair, as far as I can tell. Guanaco did not leave a message for MarkSweep until 00:35 on March 6, and that communication is not directly related to this dispute. Guanaco did not discuss the situation with MarkSweep, but did take the time to discuss the situation with {{user|Alex Law}}, {{user|MiraLuka}}, and {{user|SuperNova}} (all of whom thanked him for undoing the "damage" done by MarkSweep). Guanaco there indicated that he expected to be desysoped by the "corrupt ArbCom". [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Guanaco&diff=next&oldid=42002352] At about 06:51 on March 4, 2006, {{admin|Evilphoenix}} blocked both Guanaco and MarkSweep for 12 hours for disruption. {{admin|Friday}} unblocked Guanaco (but not MarkSweep) about 30 minutes later (at 07:28). ([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special%3ALog&type=block&user=&page=User%3AGuanaco block log of Guanaco], [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special%3ALog&type=block&user=&page=User%3AMarkSweep block log of MarkSweep]) Friday did discuss his block on both Evilphoenix's talk page and WP:AN/I. Both Guanaco and MarkSweep engaged in a high-profile, sterile edit war, involving the use of special privileges granted only to administrators (specifically, the vandalism rollback tool) without any attempt at discussion. Their actions demonstrate that both of them lack the respect for their fellow administrators that is expected of them. This situation was not urgently pressing; the involved parties could have easily taken the time to negotiate, seek support, gauge others' feelings, or seek consensus in some way. Instead, both administrators elected to pursue a sterile edit war. By doing so, both administrators demonstrated their profound lack of respect for Wikipedia, and therefore and should be stripped of their privileges. In Guanaco's case, since he has a track record of abuse of administrative privileges, he should be stripped of those privileges permanently; he should not be allowed to reapply for adminship without leave of the ArbCom or Jimbo Wales personally. MarkSweep lacks such a negative reputation, and as such he should be desysoped with leave to reapply at any time. Administrator Friday failed to remain neutral by unblocking Guanaco but not MarkSweep. Friday's other comments indicate that he was biased in this matter and should not have unblocked at all. The ArbCom should censure Friday in some manner; while a full desysopping is probably excessive, some form of censure (either a temporary desysopping for a short time or a reprimand) is in order. ====Additional comment==== I should add that this request for arbitration has '''nothing''' to do with userboxes. I brought it because two admins perpetuated a sterile edit war in an especially egregious way. The fact that it took place over userboxes has nothing to do with the wrongness of their actions. I strongly urge everyone involved to work very hard '''not''' to make this RfAr about userboxes, as down that road lies madness. === Statement by [[User:Guanaco]]=== This was an edit war. Like all edit wars, it was disruptive. I should have made an attempt to discuss this with MarkSweep, but I had the (false?) impression that he was not interested in discussion. I agreed not to continue a sterile revert war, and I will discuss this instead of continuing to revert the templates. My use of the rollback tool was merely a shortcut; I would have reverted the edits manually if necessary. I understand that revert warring is bad, and I will try to avoid it in the future. I urge the Arbitration Committee to reject this case so that MarkSweep, Zocky, Friday, Evilphoenix, and I can do more productive things with our time on Wikipedia. —[[User:Guanaco|Guan]][[User talk:Guanaco|aco]] 01:58, 6 March 2006 (UTC) Dmcdevit is not neutral in this case and should recuse himself. He has taken sides in this matter on [[Wikipedia:Administrators' noticeboard/Incidents]]. —[[User:Guanaco|Guan]][[User talk:Guanaco|aco]] 03:56, 6 March 2006 (UTC) :I don't have a conflict of interest; I just expressed criticism for the same reason I have accepted the case: it appears to be a valid claim. There are no sides to be taken. [[User:Dmcdevit|Dmcdevit]]·[[User talk:Dmcdevit|t]] 04:08, 6 March 2006 (UTC) ::Saying that it appears to be a valid claim is one thing. Stating that my actions were "disgraceful" is another. —[[User:Guanaco|Guan]][[User talk:Guanaco|aco]] 04:25, 6 March 2006 (UTC) I have requested mediation on this matter. I believe mediation would result in a much more amicable solution. —[[User:Guanaco|Guan]][[User talk:Guanaco|aco]] 04:25, 6 March 2006 (UTC) === Statement by [[User:MarkSweep]]=== In the interest of full disclosure I should point out that I've been removing superfluous categories from templates since at least February 22 without any major complaints. If it hadn't been for {{user|StrangerInParadise}} and "his" [[Template:User pro-cannabis]], which is a particularly egregious example of Wikipedia-external advocacy, all of this would have proceeded quietly. Moreover, I did not simply remove categories from templates, but in many instances did additional cleanup work. It was inappropriate for Guanaco to revert my edits ''en masse'', treating them as nothing more than vandalism. I realize that things should have stopped there, but it's hard to see one's extensive cleanup work undone just like that. I thought all of this was settled after Guanaco and I got blocked, but if this request gets accepted I only ask for one thing: please ask a clerk to closely monitor the subpages and keep this very narrowly on topic. Thanks, --[[User:MarkSweep|MarkSweep]] [[User talk:MarkSweep|(call me collect)]] 02:19, 6 March 2006 (UTC) And I don't see why Zocky and Evilphoenix are mentioned here at all. Their actions are uncontested. --[[User:MarkSweep|MarkSweep]] [[User talk:MarkSweep|(call me collect)]] 02:25, 6 March 2006 (UTC) === Statement by [[User:Friday]]=== My only involvement in this case is that I undid the block done on Guanaco. The admin whose block I undid has [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk%3AEvilphoenix&diff=42290327&oldid=42171083 said that it was OK with him], so I don't see where there's a complaint involving me here. I'll probably respond in more detail later. [[User:Friday|Friday]] [[User talk:Friday|(talk)]] 04:41, 6 March 2006 (UTC) Alright, I've thought about it more. I can think of one or two ways there could be a dispute involving me here. 1) '''Wheel warring'''. I'm glad to see the Arbcom paying attention to this. My user page explains my opinions on this matter. Read the "Wiki philsophy" section [[User:Friday#Wiki philosophy|there]] and you'll see what I mean. The most relevant bit is ''Some people are opposed to any reversal of a sysop action but I am not one of them. If I strongly feel a block is wrong, I may sometimes unblock. Generally, I'd bring it up with the blocking admin instead, but it depends on circumstances. If I see an improper deletion, I may well undelete it, without waiting a week on deletion review. I believe it's almost always poor form for someone who's action has been undone to redo it.'' I believe that this approach discourages wheel warring, whereas "admin actions should never be undone!" encourages it. This was my approach, documented on my user page, since long before this incident. If the Arbcom believes this is an inappropriate or harmful approach for an admin to take, then there may be good reason to get me to change, or (failing that) remove my sysop bit. I currently believe it's a mature and reasonable approach, but if anyone can tell me why it's harmful, I could possibly change my mind. 2)The other issue where it's been allaged that I acted inappropriately was by '''being biased'''. I unblocked Guanaco but not Mark Sweep. I'll admit I'm not particularly neutral in the "userbox war" - I have a fairly strong opinion that fighting about them is counterproductive and we shouldn't waste our time on it. But, my decision to unblock Guanaco was NOT based on him being on the "right side". It was simply that the block wasn't useful. I was afraid it would escalate the conflict. The block message on his talk page mentioned an edit war with MS on some templates. To me this looked like a one-time incident rather than a pattern of disruption. Blocks should not be punishment, they should be about damage control. So why not unblock MS also? Well, I've been seeing his name a lot lately; his pattern of edit warring on these issues was already known to me. I had no such prior knowledge about Guanaco. That said, anyone who disagreed with the MS block would have been (in my view) within their rights to undo it. If nobody chose to do so, I don't see that this has any influence on the appropriateness (or inappropriateness) of my actions. At any rate, if people are too quick to act sometimes (and it's entirely possible I was, in this case), I'd rather have people being quick to unblock than to block - it's less likely to stir up additional trouble. [[User:Friday|Friday]] [[User talk:Friday|(talk)]] 15:18, 6 March 2006 (UTC) === Statement by [[User:Zocky]]=== My connection to this case has been limited to blocking Mark for 3RR [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special%3ALog&type=block&user=Zocky&page=User%3AMarkSweep][http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:MarkSweep&diff=prev&oldid=41889797] and warning Stranger in Paradise for shouting vandalism when there was none[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:StrangerInParadise&diff=prev&oldid=41889985]. AFAIC, that was that, and unless somebody has actual complaints about my actions, I'd like to become an uninvolded non-party in this case. [[User talk:Zocky|Zocky]] | [[User:Zocky/Picture Popups|picture popups]] 03:05, 6 March 2006 (UTC) :I see that some users are trying to force this through to get ArbCom to pronounce judgments on userboxes and even basic choices about how Wikipedia community should work, i.e. the relationship between process and product. That is both outside the scope of this case and outside authority of the ArbCom, and I urge ArbCom to refuse to deliberate about those questions. [[User talk:Zocky|Zocky]] | [[User:Zocky/Picture Popups|picture popups]] 12:15, 7 March 2006 (UTC) === Statement by [[User:Evilphoenix]]=== As I said in some of the discussion I participated in about this, we need to focus as a community on building consensus and cooperation. What we do ''not'' need are edit wars, which is exactly what I saw...two editors reverting each other on controversial userboxes, so I applied an equal sided block on both, as I felt otherwise there would be no stop to it. I also think we need to worry about wheel warring, but I also don't think Friday's actions were anything remotely like a wheel war. We have the power as Admins to undo each others actions for a reason. Courtesy asks us to attempt discussion with any Admins whose actions we reverse, but sometimes that is not feasible. In this example, Friday did try to contact me, but I had already gone to bed and was therefore unavailable. What is more problematic to Wikipedia is when Administrators choose to continue an Admistrative action after being reverted. If I had responded by re-blocking Guanaco, ''that'' would have been a wheel war. We all need to respect our fellow Administrators enough not to push buttons more than once on something. However, I don't think that happened in this situation, and I have no issue with what Friday did. I have nothing further to say on this issue, as my involvement goes no further than having placed a block on both parties, and I will probably not be monitoring this RfAr. Please contact me if I can be of further assistance. Best regards, [[User:Evilphoenix|Ëvilphoenix]] [[User_talk:Evilphoenix|Burn!]] 05:54, 6 March 2006 (UTC) ==Preliminary decisions== ==== Arbitrators' opinion on hearing this matter (5/0/0/0) ==== *Accept [[User:The Epopt|➥the Epopt]] 01:51, 6 March 2006 (UTC) * Accept. [[User:Dmcdevit|Dmcdevit]]·[[User talk:Dmcdevit|t]] 03:38, 6 March 2006 (UTC) *Accept. [[User:Mindspillage|Mindspillage]] [[User talk:Mindspillage|(spill yours?)]] 04:33, 6 March 2006 (UTC) *Accept. [[User:Sam Korn|Sam Korn]] [[User talk:Sam Korn|(smoddy)]] 17:29, 6 March 2006 (UTC) *Accept. [[User:Charles Matthews|Charles Matthews]] 17:54, 6 March 2006 (UTC) ===Temporary injunction=== 1) For continuing to make disputed reversals without discussion, {{admin|Guanaco}} is prohibited from reversing another administrator's action for the duration of this arbitration. He should seek consensus and assistance at the [[WP:AN|administrators' noticeboard]] instead. :''Passed 4 to 0 at 07:05, 19 March 2006 (UTC) =Final decision= ==Principles== ===Administrators=== 1) Administrators are trusted members of the Wikipedia community and are expected to show good judgment. Administrators should in particular avoid actions that are likely to be disruptive. Administrators are not to use their tools in any dispute in which they are directly involved. :Passed 11-0 ===Edit warring=== 2) [[Wikipedia:Edit war|Edit warring]] is considered harmful, because it causes ill-will between users and negatively destabilizes articles. Editors are encourage to explore alternate methods of [[Wikipedia:Dispute resolution|dispute resolution]]. :Passed 11-0 ===Civility=== 3) Users are expected to be reasonably courteous to each other; see [[Wikipedia:Civility]], [[Wikipedia:No personal attacks]], and [[Wikipedia:Assume good faith]]. Mischaracterizations of others' edits as vandalism is a breach of civility and a failure to assume of good faith. See [[Wikipedia:Vandalism#What vandalism is not]]. :Passed 11-0 ===Communication=== 4) In order for it to function as a collaborative project, it is essential that Wikipedia's editors communicate with each other, especially when behavior is disputed. When reasonable concerns are raised, editors are expected to be responsive to criticism. Administrators in particular should be communicative and responsive, and strive for transparency in their actions. When making a controversial revert, it is important to give a relevant edit summary explaining the edit and its reasoning. :Passed 11-0 ===Disruption=== 5) Editors who are disruptive whether by edit warring or otherwise may be blocked. Persistent disruption with respect to a specific article or topic may lead to a banning from that area. :Passed 11-0 ===Speedy deletion=== 6) Pages which, in an individual administrator's judgment, conform to the [[WP:CSD|criteria for speedy deletion]] may be deleted without discussion. In general, it is good practice to take disputed deletions to [[WP:DRV|deletion review]]. The issue typically should be put up for review and consensus before a reversal is made, especially in the case that a deletion is clearly not accidental or an undeletion is clearly controversial. Persistently circumventing the review process with recreations, undeletion, or redeletions may constitute disruption. :Passed 11-0 ===Divisive or inflammatory userboxes may be speedily deleted=== 7) Templates, particularly [[Wikipedia:User boxes|userboxes]], which are divisive or inflammatory may be speedily deleted; see [[Wikipedia:Criteria for speedy deletion#Templates]]. For discussion, see [[Wikipedia talk:Criteria for speedy deletion#Comment on project page asked for links to Jimbo's opinions]], and especially [[Wikipedia talk:Criteria for speedy deletion#Regarding the new Template CSD]]. However, Jimbo Wales has urged both caution in deleting userboxes while the policy is discussed, and, in particular, restraint in reversing others' deletions or undeletions. :Passed 11-0 == Findings of fact == ===Wheel war=== 1) The persistent deletions by MarkSweep and undeletions by Guanaco, across many pages and on many different occasions, constitute a wheel war. See [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special:Log&limit=100&offset=220&type=&user=Guanaco&page= Guanaco's log] and [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special%3ALog&type=&user=MarkSweep&page= MarkSweep's log]. :Passed 11-0 ===MarkSweep misuses rollback=== 2) MarkSweep has misused his administrative rollback tool to make mass reverts of non-vandalism, in userbox-related content disputes. This occurred on multiple occasions and against various established users acting in good faith. See [[Wikipedia:Requests for arbitration/Guanaco, MarkSweep, et al/Evidence#Both Guanaco and MarkSweep engaged in an edit war using the rollback tool|Zzyzx11 evidence]] and [[Wikipedia:Requests for arbitration/Guanaco, MarkSweep, et al/Evidence#Both Guanaco and MarkSweep engaged in an edit war using the rollback tool|Sarge Baldy evidence]]. :Passed 7-2-2 ===Guanaco misuses rollback=== 3) Guanaco has misused his administrative rollback tool to make mass reverts of non-vandalism, in userbox-related content disputes. This occurred on multiple occasions and against various established users acting in good faith. He was blocked for this on March 4, and continued the behavior after the block. See [[Wikipedia:Requests for arbitration/Guanaco, MarkSweep, et al/Evidence#Both Guanaco and MarkSweep engaged in an edit war using the rollback tool|Zzyzx11 evidence]] and [[Wikipedia:Requests for arbitration/Guanaco, MarkSweep, et al/Evidence#Both Guanaco and MarkSweep engaged in an edit war using the rollback tool|Flcelloguy evidence]]. :Passed 7-2-2 ===MarkSweep has edit warred=== 4) MarkSweep has edit warred with regard to userbox templates. He has been blocked for 3RR in one instance [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special%3ALog&type=block&user=Zocky&page=User%3AMarkSweep] and for "disruptive edit warring" in another [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special%3ALog&type=block&user=Evilphoenix&page=User%3AMarkSweep]. :Passed 11-0 ===Guanaco has edit warred=== 5) Guanaco has edit warred with regard to userbox templates. He has been blocked for "disruptive edit warring" [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special%3ALog&type=block&user=Evilphoenix&page=User%3AGuanaco]. :Passed 11-0 ===Guanaco and MarkSweep are uncommunicative and unresponsive=== 6) Despite the enormous amounts of disputed edits, reverts, deletions, and undeletions that each has performed, Guanaco and MarkSweep have been uncommunicative in their actions. They have warred without attempting to resolve the situation through discussion with each other and others. They have also continued controversial reverts and deletions/undeletions despite attempts at dialogue and objections by others, and even blocks. MarkSweep: [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:MarkSweep&diff=41870824&oldid=41870807] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:MarkSweep&diff=42169348&oldid=42167476] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:MarkSweep&diff=41743747&oldid=41742656] Guanaco: [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Guanaco&diff=40310949&oldid=40232405] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Guanaco&diff=40537766&oldid=40528084] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Guanaco&diff=41992401&oldid=41977488] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Guanaco&diff=42169964&oldid=42167470] :Passed 11-0 ===Guanaco reverses administrators without discussion=== 7) Guanaco has a pattern of reversing other admins' deletions or blocks without prior notification or discussion, and without consensus. See [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special%3ALog&type=&user=Guanaco&page=User%3AWaya+sahoni] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special%3ALog&type=&user=Guanaco&page=User%3AKarmafist] and the many userbox template and category restorations. :Passed 11-0 ===Guanaco was desysopped=== 8) Guanaco was previously desysopped after failing a [[Wikipedia:Requests for adminship/Guanaco|reapplication for adminship]] required by the Arbitration Committee for misuse of administrator tools. See [[Wikipedia:Requests for arbitration/Cantus vs. Guanaco]]. :Passed 11-0 ===Guanaco is uncivil=== 9) Guanaco has referred to disputed edits by others as "vandalism". This constitutes incivility, and is an unwarranted assumption of bad faith. [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:User_Sudoku&diff=next&oldid=41635878], [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:User_UN&diff=prev&oldid=42145702] :Passed 11-0 ===Guanaco has used admin tools when involved=== 10) Guanaco inappropriately blocked MarkSweep despite their personal conflict. [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special%3ALog&type=&user=Guanaco&page=User%3AMarkSweep] :Passed 10-0 ===Friday unblocks without discussion=== 11) Administrator Friday reversed another administrator's block of Guanaco without prior discussion or consensus seeking in the matter [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special%3ALog&type=block&user=Friday&page=User%3AGuanaco]. She brought the matter to the community's attention only after performing the unblock. :Passed 6-5 ===StrangerInParadise is disruptive=== 12) On March 4, StrangerInParadise used the [[Special:Whatlinkshere]] feature to contact 43 users with a certain userbox. He spammed them with a deliberately provocative attempt to stack the ongoing userbox policy poll [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special:Contributions&target=StrangerInParadise&offset=20060305015959&limit=200&namespace=3]. The messages, headed "Your userpage was briefly delisted by a rogue admin" constitute personal attacks [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Wikster72&diff=prev&oldid=42263868]. StrangerInParadise was subsequently blocked [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special:Log&type=block&page=User%3AStrangerInParadise]. :Passed 10-0 ===StrangerInParadise is uncivil=== 13) In addition to the personal attacks made in his spam messages, StrangerInParadise has persisted in incivility and referring to other users with whom he is in a dispute as vandals or as performing vandalism ([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:User_pro-cannabis&diff=41848813&oldid=41828414] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:User_pro-cannabis&diff=41868017&oldid=41864702] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:User_pro-cannabis&diff=41874502&oldid=41868049] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia_talk:Userbox_policy_poll&diff=prev&oldid=42451911] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia_talk:Userbox_policy_poll&diff=prev&oldid=42599007] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:StrangerInParadise&diff=prev&oldid=42315147], [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Nightstallion&diff=41879529&oldid=41879300] and more), despite warnings to the contrary [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:StrangerInParadise&diff=41889985&oldid=prev] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk%3AStrangerInParadise&diff=42265249&oldid=42262030], [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:StrangerInParadise&diff=42266508&oldid=42265249]. These constitute both personal attacks and unwarranted assumptions of bad faith. See [[Wikipedia:Administrators%27_noticeboard/IncidentArchive79#StrangerInParadise_spambot_spamming_userpages|discussion on Administrators' noticeboard]]. :Passed 11-0 ==Remedies== ''Note: All remedies that refer to a period of time, for example to a ban of X months or a revert parole of Y months, are to run concurrently unless otherwise stated.'' ===Guanaco desysopped=== 1) For his poor judgment, uncommunicativeness, wheel warring, and other misuses of administrator tools including rollback and blocking powers, Guanaco is desysopped. In view of his previous desysopping, he may not request to have his adminship restored. Guanaco may regain the tools via a new [[WP:RFA|request for adminship]]. :Passed 11-0 ::Amended on 13:45, 27 August 2014 (UTC) ===StrangerInParadise placed on personal attack parole=== 2) StrangerInParadise is placed on standard personal attack parole for one year. If he makes any edits which are judged by an administrator to be personal attacks, then he may be temporarily banned for a short time of up to one week. This remedy is to be interpreted broadly to include unwarranted assumptions of bad faith. After five such blocks, the maximum block time is increased to one year. This remedy shall apply to all accounts. :Passed 10-0 ===Restricted with regard to userboxes=== 3) If, in the view of any three uninvolved administrators, Guanaco, MarkSweep, or StrangerInParadise are disruptive with regard to userboxes, or related talk, category, template, or project pages, they may be banned from all userbox-related pages for a period of up to a year. Violations of a ban imposed under this remedy may lead to short blocks of up to two weeks for repeat offenses. All blocks and bans should be recorded at [[Wikipedia:Requests for arbitration/Guanaco, MarkSweep, et al#Log of blocks and bans]]. This remedy is to apply per person and not per account. :Passed 10-0 ===MarkSweep banned from userboxes=== 4) As he has shown consistently poor judgment when dealing with userboxes, MarkSweep is banned from editing and taking any administrative action with regard to userboxes. If he violates this remedy, he may be briefly blocked, up to a week in the case of repeat offenses. All blocks should be noted at [[Wikipedia:Requests for arbitration/Guanaco%2C MarkSweep%2C et al#Log of blocks and bans]]. :Passed 10-0 ===MarkSweep cautioned=== 5) MarkSweep is strongly cautioned to use the administrator's rollback tool only when reverting [[Wikipedia:vandalism|vandalism]]. :Passed 9-0-2 ==Subsequent amendments== ====StrangerInParadise restricted to one user account==== StrangerInParadise is restricted to one user account. Any sockpuppet accounts will be blocked indefinitely and the main account blocked for up to 48 hours if this is violated. :Support: :# [[User:Mindspillage|Mindspillage]] [[User talk:Mindspillage|(spill yours?)]] 14:39, 28 April 2006 (UTC) :# [[User:Fred Bauder|Fred Bauder]] 14:42, 28 April 2006 (UTC) :# [[User:The Epopt|➥the Epopt]] 14:46, 28 April 2006 (UTC) :# [[User:Jdforrester|James F.]] [[User talk:Jdforrester|(talk)]] 17:04, 28 April 2006 (UTC) :# [[User:Charles Matthews|Charles Matthews]] 15:11, 30 April 2006 (UTC) :# [[User:Jayjg|Jayjg ]][[User_talk:Jayjg|(talk)]] 01:46, 1 May 2006 (UTC) :# [[User:Morven|Matthew Brown (Morven)]] ([[User talk:Morven|T]]:[[Special:Contributions/Morven|C]]) 23:27, 4 May 2006 (UTC) :Oppose: :Abstain: : Passed effective 23:27, 4 May 2006 (UTC) ===Guanaco desysopped (amendment)=== The second sentence of remedy 1 of the ''[[Wikipedia:Requests for arbitration/Guanaco, MarkSweep, et al|Guanaco, MarkSweep, et al]]'' case, currently reading: {{ivmbox|In view of his previous desysopping, he may not request to have his adminship restored.}} is vacated and replaced with the following: {{ivmbox|Guanaco may regain the tools via a new [[WP:RFA|request for adminship]].}} :''Passed 10 to 0 by [[Special:Permalink/623025911#Amendment_request:_Guanaco.2C_MarkSweep.2C_et_al|motion]], 13:45, 27 August 2014 (UTC)'' ==Log of blocks and bans== Here log any block, ban or extension under any remedy in this decision. cases.title: Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Case/Gun control
cases.content:
{{Casenav|case name=Gun control|clerk1=Penwhale|clerk2=Bbb23|draft arb=Seraphimblade|draft arb2=Roger Davies|active=12|inactive=2|recused=0}}
A previous RFC on this article was procedurally closed on January 26th by [[User:Nyttend]] because of this active arbitration case. See [[Talk:Gun_control#Authoritarianism_and_gun_control_RFC]] for more information.
'''Case Opened''' on 18:44, 5 Jan 2014 (UTC) '''Case closed''' on 20:00, 30 April 2014 (UTC) '''Case amended by [[Special:Permalink/685759243#Amendment request: Gun control (Gaijin42)|motion]]''' on 01:48, 15 October 2015 (UTC) '''Case amended by [[Special:Permalink/975119648#North8000 restrictions: Motion|motion]]''' on 21:40, 26 August 2020 (UTC) '''Case amended by [[#Motion:_contentious_topic_designation_(December_2022)|motion]]''' on 21:36, 14 December 2022 (UTC)
Watchlist all case (and talk) pages: [{{SERVER}}{{SCRIPTPATH}}/index.php?title={{FULLPAGENAMEE}}&action=watch '''Front'''], [{{SERVER}}{{SCRIPTPATH}}/index.php?title={{FULLPAGENAMEE}}/Evidence&action=watch '''Ev.'''], [{{SERVER}}{{SCRIPTPATH}}/index.php?title={{FULLPAGENAMEE}}/Workshop&action=watch '''Wshp.'''], [{{SERVER}}{{SCRIPTPATH}}/index.php?title={{FULLPAGENAMEE}}/Proposed_decision&action=watch '''PD.''']
The case is now closed. Editors may edit the [[#Log of blocks, bans, and restrictions]] as needed, but the other content of this page may not be edited except by clerks or arbitrators. Please raise any questions about this decision at [[Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Clarification and Amendment]], any general questions at [[Wikipedia talk:Arbitration Committee]], and report violations of the remedies passed in the decision to [[Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Enforcement]]. == Case information == === Involved parties === *{{userlinks|Gaijin42}}, ''filing party'' *{{userlinks|AndyTheGrump}} *{{userlinks|Goethean}} *{{userlinks|Justanonymous}} *{{userlinks|North8000}} *{{userlinks|ROG5728}} *{{userlinks|Anythingyouwant}} *{{userlinks|Hipocrite}} ===Prior dispute resolution=== *[[Talk:Gun_control#Authoritarianism_and_gun_control_RFC]] (ongoing RFC/Debate) *[[Talk:Gun_control/Archive_3#RFC:_Section_on_Association_of_Gun_control_with_authoritarianism]] *[[Wikipedia:Dispute_resolution_noticeboard/Gun_Control]] *[[Wikipedia:Administrators%27_noticeboard/Archive251#Conflict_around_Gun_control]] *[[Wikipedia_talk:Dispute_resolution_noticeboard/Archive_13#Gun_Control_DR.2FN]] *[[Talk:Gun_control/Archive_5#RFC]] == Preliminary statements == === Statement by Gaijin42 === Extended controversial edit war and content dispute. Nazi use of gun control is a historical fact, documented by COPIOUS primary and secondary sources [[User:Gaijin42/GunControlArguments]] (including primary sources of the laws, orders, memos, diaries etc of the Nazis, historical secondary news accounts confirming the events etc. These historical facts are a common theme in the gun control debate being used internationally by gun rights proponents, and criticized by gun control proponents. (many books, magazine articles, scholarly articles etc on both sides) Numerous dispute resolution avenues have been explored, all resulting in no consensus and a stalemated edit war running over months. ArbCom does not generally take sides in content disputes, but here I think the core problem is differing opinions on policy, therefore policy clarification is required which will enable parties to work on the same page.[[WP:NPOV]] says all significant viewpoints should be included in a neutral manner, based on [[WP:RS]] and [[WP:V]] . After significant debate and edit warring and extended page protection, where Andy continued the edit war immediately upon page protection ending, the following text was [[WP:BOLD]]ly added by myself [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&curid=44276&diff=589026452&oldid=589025992] and promptly removed - note that everything is sourced to scholarly articles, books, and neutrally presented including more text on the opposing viewpoint.. The history is verified. The peoples opinions about the history is verified. The counter arguments are verified. (Admittedly over the course of the edit war, there have been poor versions of text included, but the war prevented a standard BRD improvement cycle since the content has been repeatedly deleted.) ('''update''' subsequently the article has been re-protected for a month, with the proposed text having been reinserted by another editor. I'm sure others may claim [[WP:WRONGVERSION]] but it provides an opportunity for people to discuss the specific text and sources in that version and how policies apply) [[User:Gaijin42|Gaijin42]] ([[User talk:Gaijin42|talk]]) 23:02, 3 January 2014 (UTC) Questions for clarification * To what degree does consensus determine what [[WP:FRINGE]] is. Are [[WP:RS]] required to label something as fringe, or is [[WP:OR]] sufficient * to what degree can [[WP:FRINGE]] be applied at all to political opinions based on uncontested facts (even the RS that argue against the gun lobby admit to the core history) * to what degree can fringe be applied to political controversies where there is no "truth" * [[WP:RS]] says that "reliable sources are not required to be neutral, unbiased, or objective. " * As admitted by the sources in the counter argument, the confiscation history is verifiably true, and the opinions are held by a large number of people (particularly in the US, but to a lesser degree internationally as well) * Although there is no globalize policy/guideline, AND the content does reference international viewpoint, the argument has been raised that since this is primarily a US argument it is unfit for the general gun control article. To what degree does having a global overview require excluding viewpoints which are notable in a particular country? [[User:Gaijin42|Gaijin42]] ([[User talk:Gaijin42|talk]]) 20:53, 3 January 2014 (UTC) The core editors in opposition have completely avoided all attempts at building consensus, and insist that the information must be deleted completely. No sources are provided for their assertions, just rhetoric saying that because we can't list the opinions, because by definition anyone who mentions those opinions is fringe. [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=586120554&oldid=586117719] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=586350781&oldid=586349938] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=586685069&oldid=586684972] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=586701316&oldid=586701237] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=587935331&oldid=587934684] Or attempting to procedurally invalidate any attempt at building consensus with mutually contradictory requirements for RFCs [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=560778955&oldid=560778437] [[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Gun_control#This_RfC_appears_to_be_invalid]] That to include secondary sources A, you must find secondary source B discussing source A (also equating opinions about established historical facts to UFOs) [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=586703333&oldid=586701791] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=586701316&oldid=586701237] Or during a discussion about if content is sourced sufficiently, removing sources that directly confirm the facts under contention [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=587623770&oldid=587619937] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=586716977&oldid=586702762] Or deleting the section entirely repeatedly while it is the subject of an RFC and that have been in the article for months [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=587623958&oldid=587623770] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=587790798&oldid=587682531] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=587925421&oldid=587877372] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=587940603&oldid=587934496] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=587941033&oldid=587940916] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=587945382&oldid=587944962] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=587946768&oldid=587946457] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=587931606&oldid=587926148] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=589025799&oldid=589025366] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=589026747&oldid=589026551] Attempts to redefine the topic of the article to exclude unwanted material [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=553069396&oldid=553067662] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=553259757&oldid=553259328] complete failure to provide any specific guidance on what part of a policy apply or which particular bits of content are in violation [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=589023119&oldid=589023062] attempting to declare by fiat that notable expers on gun control publshing in respected academic journals is not an RS by fiat. [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=587640453&oldid=587640371] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=586676871&oldid=586676583] Saying "we should emulate this list of neutral sources",as an argument for exclusion, and not noticing that several of those sources explicitly cover this material [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=586376420&oldid=586376343] Acknowledging the controversial pov as a significant minority view and then saying it should be ignored directly in opposition of [[WP:NPOV]] [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=586543772&oldid=586541802] @Just anonymous, you mentioned the [[Gun Control]] vs [[Gun Politics]] debate. The politics article has been renamed (without issue it appears) to [[Overview of gun laws by nation]] since that is an accurate description of the content of that article. This leaves a clear separation between an overview of each countries laws (with links to the detailed articles where appropriate), and a high level discussion of the topic itself, and the arguments regarding effectiveness, side effects, rights etc as a whole and not specific to one particular implementation. In this case we have multiple countries discussing Germany's history as a point in ongoing debates, so it does not makes sense to partition that information under a single country (although the details and specifics of the german law, as opposed the the arguments about the laws should move into the germany article) [[User:Gaijin42|Gaijin42]] ([[User talk:Gaijin42|talk]]) 22:34, 3 January 2014 (UTC) {{u|edChem}} I am quite baffled by your statement. There is no misrepresentation of sources. Nowhere is it stated or implied that the authors hold or endorse the gun rights view. Reliable sources are regularly used to document viewpoints other than the author's own. Indeed, this is probably preferred! the origin of the opinion is a primary source. Someone else commenting on that opinion is secondary, and shows that the first person's opinion was notable enough to be discussed. The AU article, which points to page 221 in the ref begins "Internationally, the gun lobby is quite fond of comparing gun control agenda with Hitler in pre WWII Germany" and then proceeds to name several individuals and groups that had propagated that argument. That content directly backs the statements made in the article text. For the Canadian source, you yourself quoted the exact statements that back the content in the article. Any ambiguity or confusion in this statement could easily be resolved via normal BRD improvements and is not an issue for ArbCom. If you would like to add the authors in as international viewpoints arguing against the meme (along with Halbrook and Spitzer) I have no objection. [[User:Gaijin42|Gaijin42]] ([[User talk:Gaijin42|talk]]) 13:53, 4 January 2014 (UTC) Regarding godwinning or argumentum ad hitlerum - It may be the case that the NRA et al have done so, but their doing so is notable and influential in the gun control debate internationally, and should be neutrally covered (as the current text does). Our covering that usage and debate is not endorsing that view any more than when Slate, Mother Jones, or others discuss the arguments (and then they do generally go on to take sides against the argument ;)) [[User:Gaijin42|Gaijin42]] ([[User talk:Gaijin42|talk]]) 16:33, 4 January 2014 (UTC) === Statement by AndyTheGrump === It might appear from the above statement that much of what Gaijin42 is asking could perhaps be described as a 'content dispute', and thus outside the remit of arbitration. There are however core policy issues, and issues relating to the ongoing behaviour of particular contributors, that need resolving. The immediate locus of the dispute is whether particular material relating to firearms regulation in Nazi Germany is appropriate in our article entitled 'gun control', but the issues are of wider relevance, and have consequences for other articles - indeed, it is my position that this dispute raises fundamental questions regarding article neutrality throughout Wikipedia. The specifics are that the material explicitly linking Nazi Germany and the Holocaust with 'gun control'/firearms regulation issues is exclusively derived from partisan pro-gun lobbyists (almost entirely American), and is entirely unsupported by mainstream historiography. It is true enough that a few raw historical 'facts' - that Nazi Germany passed certain laws relating to firearms - can be sourced elsewhere, but no source has ever been provided from beyond the partisan gun lobby which states either that (a) Nazi firearms regulations are of any particular significance within the broader topic of firearms regulation on an international level (the supposed scope of our article), or (b) that such regulations are of any significance in the broader context of the Holocaust. It is my opinion regarding (a) that, except possibly in the context of an article on the U.S. gun debate, the complete lack of mainstream historographic support makes any discussion of the partisan pseudohistorical arguments of a particular faction in an internal debate in one country entirely undue, and that inclusion of such material violates WP:NPOV policy by giving weight (and credence) to a fringe viewpoint propagated for the purposes of a debate unconnected with the supposed topic - a viewpoint explicitly rejected as 'cherry-picked', 'tendentious' and 'decontextualised' by at least one academic writer actually cited on the article talk page ''as a reliable source'' by a contributor arguing for inclusion of the 'Nazi' material (said contributor having 'picked' said source rather selectively him/herself...). More fundamental though, is the fact that this viewpoint involves (b) assertions regarding the history of Holocaust. It hardly needs to be said that such a sensitive issue needs careful treatment, and it is my assertion that if Wikipedia is to have any credibility at all, it needs to ensure that ''content relating to the Holocaust'' (regardless of where it is located) ''needs to be sourced to historians of the Holocaust'' (of which there are no shortage), rather than to non-historian partisans engaged in debates regarding other places, and other times. ''This'' is the fundamental question - is it appropriate for an article (any article) to be promoting fringe theories unsupported (and rejected) by academia regarding the Holocaust? And if not, is it appropriate that those promoting such theories should be permitted to continue to do so? If we can't get this right, we may as well give up... [[User:AndyTheGrump|AndyTheGrump]] ([[User talk:AndyTheGrump|talk]]) 21:49, 3 January 2014 (UTC) :Just a brief comment on the claim by ROG5728 that "no theory is mentioned in the article, so this content could not possibly fall under WP:FRINGE, since the content is not a theory". This assertion is demonstrably false, given that material ''posted by ROG5728'' [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=589047433&oldid=589046583] explicitly states that "Gun rights advocates... have argued that these laws were an enabling factor in The Holocaust...". A charitable explanation for this misstatement is probably that ROG5728 hadn't actually read the material in question. [[User:AndyTheGrump|AndyTheGrump]] ([[User talk:AndyTheGrump|talk]]) 00:11, 4 January 2014 (UTC) ::One other point. I shall of course have more to say on the assertions made by Gaijin42 concerning diffs in the initial statement later, should this case be accepted for arbitration, but I think that it should be noted that at least two of the diffs concern a contributor not named in this case - [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=553259757&oldid=553259328] and [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=553069396&oldid=553067662], both posted by [[User:Steeletrap]]. It seems to me entirely improper to be citing such diffs as evidence without informing the contributor - I shall of course do so myself. [[User:AndyTheGrump|AndyTheGrump]] ([[User talk:AndyTheGrump|talk]]) 17:57, 4 January 2014 (UTC) === Statement by Justanonymous === Esteemed arbitrators, editors and contributors, I will be the first to accept that I have never been here before and hope not to come here often - so I hope I do justice to this forum and I beg you indulge my inexperience. I have read the Arbitration guidelines in an attempt to try to do this forum justice but I am far from an expert here. To me, at the heart of this dispute lie some core and fundamental differences that we could use help in arbitrating: '''Should the Gun Control Article Exist?''' - Some editors believe it should not and that it should be folded into some other topic like [[gun politics]]. Some editors believe it should stand as its own article. My contention has been that the article should exist for the following reasons: #the term is widely used, it is found in the dictionary http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/gun%20control. #other substitute terms proposed are not found in dictionaries and are less accepted to encompass gun control. #searches on google return millions of records on the subject and major news media have entire sections devoted to the topic. #there are numerous books and academic papers that use the term. '''What Content Should go into the article?''' - There is also a disagreement over what content should go into the article and a lesser argument over organization. Should the actions of repressive regimes disarming their populations count as ''gun control'', should ''international aspects of small arms trade'' be part of the topic of gun control? These are questions and they don't have agreement. #I believe that at the core of the disagreement rests the definition of '''gun control'''. So, some editors believe that some of the actions taken by regimes such as the Nazi Regime and the United States against slaves was not '''gun control''' per se. Other editors disagree. [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=&diff=prev&oldid=587854266], [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=&diff=prev&oldid=586700117], [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=&diff=prev&oldid=586362286], [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=&diff=prev&oldid=542106824], [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=&diff=prev&oldid=541931834], [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=&diff=prev&oldid=539905907]. :''Passed 11 to 0 at 19:57, 30 April 2014 (UTC)'' ===North8000=== 6) {{userlinks|North8000}} has engaged in: * [[Wikipedia:Sock puppetry#Editing while logged out|Editing while logged out]] seemingly to either avoid sanction and/or to escape scrutiny. ([https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=542073847&oldid=542073242], [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=542088087&oldid=542084656], [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=552793617&oldid=552793291], [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gun_control&diff=552817168&oldid=552802325]) * [[Wikipedia:What Wikipedia is not#Wikipedia is not a battleground|Battleground conduct]] with failure to [[Wikipedia:Disruptive editing#Failure or refusal to "get the point"|listen]]: [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=prev&oldid=552925053], [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Gun_control&diff=prev&oldid=588333137] * and [[Wikipedia:What Wikipedia is not#Wikipedia is not a soapbox or means of promotion|Soapboxing]] by placing [[Wikipedia:Neutral point of view#Due and undue weight|undue weight]] on inappropriate material in articles; The earliest he may request a lifting of the site-ban is twelve months from the passing of this remedy. Should fresh [[Wikipedia:Sock puppetry#Inappropriate uses of alternative accounts|infringements of the sock puppetry policy]] occur after the passing of this remedy, the twelve-month site-ban will be reset to run from the date of the last such infringement. Additionally, North8000 is indefinitely prohibited from making any edit about, and from editing any page relating to, [[#Gun control: definition|gun control]] broadly construed. The topic-ban in the [[Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Case/Tea Party movement#North8000 topic-banned|Tea Party case]] remains in force. :''Passed 11 to 0 at 19:57, 30 April 2014 (UTC)'' ::The gun control editing restriction and topic-ban from the Tea Party case has been suspended by [[Special:Permalink/975119648#North8000 restrictions: Motion|motion]] at 20:49, 26 August 2020 (UTC). If not reimposed within one year at [[WP:ARCA]], the topic-ban and editing restriction will expire. ===ROG5728 (topic-ban)=== 8) [[User:ROG5728|ROG5728]] is indefinitely prohibited from making any edit about, and all pages relating to, [[#Scope of remedies|gun control]] broadly construed. :''Passed 10 to 0 at 19:57, 30 April 2014 (UTC)'' ===Appeal of topic bans === 9) Topic bans imposed in this decision may be appealed no less than twelve months from case closure and a minimum of twelve months thereafter. For purposes of this remedy, any request to have the sanction reconsidered, modified, loosened, or lifted entirely, shall be considered an appeal. :''Passed 9 to 0 at 19:57, 30 April 2014 (UTC)'' == Enforcement == {{Arbitration standard provisions}} ==Amendments== ===October 2015=== {{User|Gaijin42}}'s topic ban from gun control-related edits imposed as Remedy 4 of the Gun control case is suspended for a period of one year. During the period of suspension, this topic ban may be reinstated by any uninvolved administrator as an arbitration enforcement action should Gaijin42 fail to adhere to Wikipedia editing standards in the area previously covered by the topic ban. Appeal of such a reinstatement would follow the normal arbitration enforcement appeals process. After one year from the date of passage of this motion, if the topic ban has not been reinstated or any reinstatements have been successfully appealed, the topic ban will be lifted. :''Passed 7 to 0 with 1 abstention by [[Special:Permalink/685759243#Motion: Gaijin42 topic ban suspension|motion]] at 01:55, 15 October 2015 (UTC)'' === North8000 restrictions: Motion (August 2020) === {{userlinks|North8000}} was restricted by motion in December 2016 ([[Special:PermanentLink/756686514#Motion_regarding_North8000|Motion regarding North80000]]). Recognizing North8000's productive contributions and renewed voluntary commitments, the restrictions are suspended for one year, during which time the restrictions may be re-imposed (individually or entirely) upon request to [[WP:ARCA]] if warranted. Any restrictions not reimposed will automatically expire at the end of the one year period. :''Passed 8 to 0 by [[Special:Permalink/975119648#North8000 restrictions: Motion|motion]] at 20:49, 26 August 2020 (UTC)'' === Motion: contentious topic designation (December 2022) === {{ivmbox|1=[[#Scope of remedies|Gun control]] is designated as a [[Wikipedia:Contentious topics|contentious topic]].}} {{hatnote|1=As part of the [[WP:CT2022|2022 adoption of the contentious topics procedure]], the Arbitration Committee adopted the following [[Wikipedia:Arbitration_Committee/Discretionary_sanctions/2021-22_review#Administrative_provisions|motion]] to re-designate existing discretionary sanctions remedies as contentious topic designations.}} {{ivmbox|1= Each reference to the prior [[WP:AC/DS|discretionary sanctions procedure]] shall be treated as a reference to the [[WP:AC/CT|contentious topics procedure]]. The arbitration clerks are directed to amend all existing remedies authorizing discretionary sanctions to instead designate contentious topics. }} :''Passed 10 to 0 with 1 abstention by [[Wikipedia:Arbitration_Committee/Discretionary_sanctions/2021-22_review#Administrative_provisions|motion]] at 21:36, 14 December 2022 (UTC)'' ==Log of blocks, bans, and restrictions== {{Wikipedia:Arbitration Committee/Enforcement log section}} {{cot|Old log entries}} Any block, restriction, ban, or sanction performed under the authorisation of a remedy for this case must be logged in this section. cases.content:
<big>'''Case Opened''' on 21:50, 18 October 2006 (UTC)</big>  

<big>'''Case Closed''' on 18:02, 4 November 2006 (UTC)</big>  

Please do not edit this page directly unless you wish to become a participant in this request. (All participants are subject to Arbitration Committee decisions, and the ArbCom will consider each participant's role in the dispute.) Comments are very welcome on the [[Wikipedia talk:{{PAGENAME}}|Talk page]], and will be read, in full. Evidence, no matter who can provide it, is very welcome at [[/Evidence]]. Evidence is more useful than comments. 

Arbitrators will be working on evidence and suggesting proposed decisions at [[/Workshop]] and voting on  proposed decisions at [[/Proposed decision]]. 

==Involved parties==
<!--provide links to the user page of each party and to all accounts they have edited with. Briefly summarize case. No details. for users use form {{Userlinks|user name}}, for administrators use {{Admin|user name}}-->

* {{admin|Thatcher131}}
* {{admin|Golden Wattle}}
* {{admin|Longhair}}

'''IPs the editor has used in the last month (dynamic ISP, probably dial-up):'''
:*{{userlinks|203.54.9.161}}

'''Articles involved'''
