[[User:Shell_Kinney|Shell]] [[User_talk:Shell_Kinney|babelfish]] 20:57, 9 February 2011 (UTC) *'''Accept''' Bit late to the party at this point. Let's pretend I have something witty to say with regards to the above. [[User:David Fuchs|Der Wohltemperierte Fuchs]]([[User talk:David Fuchs|talk]]) 23:02, 9 February 2011 (UTC) *'''Accept''' [[User:John Vandenberg|John Vandenberg]] '''([[User talk:John Vandenberg|chat]])''' 00:22, 10 February 2011 (UTC) * '''Accept'''  [[User:Roger Davies|'''Roger''']] [[User talk:Roger Davies|'''talk''']] 08:41, 10 February 2011 (UTC) *'''Accept'''. - [[User:Mailer diablo|Mailer Diablo]] 15:56, 10 February 2011 (UTC) ===Temporary injunction (none)=== =Final decision= ''All numbering based on [[/Proposed decision]], where vote counts and comments are also available.'' ==Principles== ===Role of the Committee=== 1.2) It is not the role of the Arbitration Committee to rule on good-faith content disputes between editors. :''Passed 9 to 0 at 00:25, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Purpose of Wikipedia=== 2) The purpose of Wikipedia is to create a high-quality, free-content encyclopedia in an atmosphere of camaraderie and mutual respect among contributors. Use of the encyclopedia to advance [[Wikipedia:What Wikipedia is not|personal agendas]]—such as [[Wikipedia:SOAP|advocacy or propaganda]] and [[Wikipedia:BATTLE|philosophical, ideological, religious or political dispute]] – or to publish or promote [[Wikipedia:No original research|original research]] or [[WP:FRINGE|fringe theories that have not gained widespread acceptance]] is prohibited. :''Passed 12 to 0 at 00:25, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Articles should be widely understandable === 3) From [[WP:TECHNICAL]]: articles in Wikipedia should be understandable to the widest possible audience. For most articles, this means understandable to a general audience. Every reasonable attempt should be made to ensure that material is presented in the most widely understandable manner possible. :''Passed 12 to 0 at 00:25, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Neutral point of view=== 4.2) Article content must be presented from a [[WP:NPOV|neutral point of view]]. Editors should ensure that the reporting of different views on a subject adequately reflects the relative levels of support for those views, and that it does not give a false impression of parity, or give [[WP:UNDUE|undue weight]] to a particular view. :''Passed 12 to 0 at 00:25, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Editorial process=== 5) Wikipedia works by building consensus through the use of polite discussion—involving the wider community, if necessary—and dispute resolution, rather than through adversarial editing. Sustained editorial conflict or edit-warring is not an appropriate method of resolving disputes. :''Passed 12 to 0 at 00:25, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Conduct and decorum=== 6) Wikipedia users are expected to behave reasonably, calmly, and courteously in their interactions with other users, and to approach even difficult situations in a dignified fashion and with a constructive and collaborative outlook. Editors are expected to be reasonably courteous to one another, even during disputes. Unseemly or confrontational conduct, such as personal attacks, incivility, and unwarranted assumptions of bad faith, is prohibited. :''Passed 11 to 0 at 00:25, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Tendentious editing=== 7) Users who [[Wikipedia:Tendentious editing|disrupt the editing]] of articles by engaging in sustained attacks on other editors or inflammatory comments may be banned from the affected articles. In extreme cases they may be banned from the site. :''Passed 12 to 0 at 00:25, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Good faith and disruption === 8) Inappropriate behavior driven by good intentions is still inappropriate. Editors acting in good faith may still be sanctioned when their actions are disruptive. :''Passed 11 to 1 at 00:25, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' === Use of article talk pages === 9) The purpose of a Wikipedia [[Wikipedia:TALK|talk page]] is to provide space for editors to discuss changes to its associated article or project page. Article talk pages should not be used by editors as platforms for their personal views on a subject, nor for proposing unpublished solutions, forwarding original ideas, redefining terms, or so forth (see [[Wikipedia:What Wikipedia is not#Wikipedia is not a publisher of original thought]]). Although more general discussion may be permissible in some circumstances, it will not be tolerated when it becomes [[Wikipedia:TE|tendentious]], overwhelms the page, impedes productive work, or is otherwise [[Wikipedia:DE|disruptive]]. :''Passed 12 to 0 at 00:25, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Expert editors and original research === 10) Expert editors with published resources are welcome on Wikipedia, and are free to include references to their own published works, if they meet the standards of [[WP:RS|reliable sources]]. However, the guidelines concerning [[WP:COI|conflicts of interest]] must be observed, and where there is a dispute as to the use or interpretation of such sources, consensus must be gained for their inclusion. :''Passed 10 to 0 with 2 abstentions at 00:25, 25 March 2011 (UTC) ===Mathematics (use of sources)=== 11.4) If editors disagree on how to express a problem and/or solution in mathematics, citations to reliable published sources that both are directly related to the topic of the article and directly support the material as presented must be supplied by the editor(s) who wishes to include the material. Novel derivations, applications or conclusions that cannot be supported by sources are likely to constitute [[WP:OR|original research]] within the definition used by the English Wikipedia. :''Passed 10 to 0 with 1 abstention at 00:25, 25 March 2011 (UTC) ===Article probation=== 12) Articles may be placed on probation by the Arbitration Committee or the community. When an article is under probation, editors making disruptive edits may be subject to various administrative sanctions, depending on the terms of probation. :''Passed 12 to 0 at 00:25, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ==Findings of fact== ===Statement of the dispute (coverage and presentation) === 1) The Monty Hall problem started life as an example of probability theory, intended for the wider public as well as students, and expressed in terms of a popular game show. Since then, it has become a staple of probability theorists. This dispute centres on how to present the various forms of both the question and the answer, so as to provide complete coverage of all the facets of the problem, without overwhelming the general reader. :''Passed 10 to 1 at 00:30, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Statement of the dispute (external factors) === 2) The Monty Hall problem is unusual in that while there are many scholarly sources, the key source containing the best known and most often quoted formulation of the problem is a popular one. The solution used by this source and sources derived from it uses a simple approach to demonstrate the outcome. In the literature, some proponents of the the more complex Bayesian formulations of the advanced probability version argue that the simple solution is 'wrong'. :''Passed 10 to 1 at 00:30, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Statement of dispute (two camps)=== 3) Editors have largely fallen into two camps - those who wish to give equal or higher weight to the 'simple' solutions contained within the popular literature, and those who wish to minimise those solutions on the grounds that they are 'wrong'. No party wishes to exclude information about the problem and solutions as presented in higher probability theory, although there is dispute as to how much of this information should be included in the article, and how it should be presented. :''Passed 10 to 1 at 00:30, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Article has attracted expert editors=== 4) The article has attracted a high number of expert editors, some of whom have published material of their own on the problem. :''Passed 12 to 0 at 00:30, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Article has been target of original research=== 5) The talkpage, and at times the article, has contained a considerable amount of derivation from first principles, in an effort to explain the higher aspects of probability theory ([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Monty_Hall_problem&diff=348710846&oldid=348679562#Mathematical_formulation]—[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Monty_Hall_problem&oldid=418812215#Mathematical_formulation_section incorrect derivation from first principles]; [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Monty_Hall_problem&oldid=418812215#N_doors_and_biased_choice OR] by [[User:Rich Farmbrough|Rich Farmbrough]], who is not listed as a party). :''Passed 11 to 1 at 00:30, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Glkanter === ====Tendentious editing and Conduct during the case==== 6) {{user|Glkanter}} has engaged in tendentious editing, albeit that this may have been with good faith intentions, and has engaged in poor conduct during this case.([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Monty_Hall_problem&diff=prev&oldid=376455039],[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Monty_Hall_problem&diff=next&oldid=376576965][http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Monty_Hall_problem&diff=next&oldid=368429205];[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Monty_Hall_problem&diff=269139028&oldid=269132158 statement repeated four times in different places];[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Gill110951&diff=next&oldid=410169437#Yes_or_no_please.2C_Glkanter]) :''Passed 12 to 0 at 00:30, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ====Personal attacks==== 6.1) Glkanter has engaged in personal attacks against other editors.([https://secure.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/w/index.php?title=Special:Undelete&target=User%3AGlkanter×tamp=20110314185848&diff=prev],[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia_talk:Arbitration/Requests/Case/Monty_Hall_problem/Workshop&diff=prev&oldid=417323886],[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Monty_Hall_problem&diff=271249038&oldid=271235601 describes another editor as garbage],[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk%3AGlkanter&diff=380714854],[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Monty_Hall_problem/Arguments&diff=prev&oldid=272541082 describes Rick Block as Jello],[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:Monty_Hall_problem&diff=330318661&oldid=330317073]) :''Passed 9 to 0 with 2 abstentions at 00:30, 25 March 2011 (UTC) ===Nijdam === 7) {{user|Nijdam}} has engaged in tendentious editing, particularly with regard to how the article represents the popular, simple explanations for the outcome of the problem ([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Monty_Hall_problem&diff=prev&oldid=368429205],[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Monty_Hall_problem&diff=prev&oldid=376576965],[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Gill110951&diff=next&oldid=410169437#Nijdam.27s_responses],[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Case/Monty_Hall_problem/Workshop&diff=prev&oldid=415379438]). His conduct during the case has been poor. :''Passed 12 to 0 at 00:30, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Rick Block=== 8) {{user|Rick Block}} has displayed [[Wikipedia:Ownership of articles|ownership]] of the article, and has been excessively controlling of both content and presentation ([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk%3AMonty_Hall_problem&action=historysubmit&diff=196657734&oldid=196565315][http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Monty_Hall_problem&diff=281837644&oldid=281821057], pick any archive of the talkpage). :''Passed 8 to 0 with 4 abstentions at 00:30, 25 March 2011 (UTC) ===Gill110951=== 9) {{user|Gill110951}} has used his experience of editing and discussing this article to provide material for published research,[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk%3AGill110951&action=historysubmit&diff=401816929&oldid=401815717] which he has then introduced into the article.[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Monty_Hall_problem&diff=414216390&oldid=414214347][http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Monty_Hall_problem&diff=396673431&oldid=396566441][http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Monty_Hall_problem&diff=396673624&oldid=396673537] :''Passed 10 to 1 with 1 abstention at 00:30, 25 March 2011 (UTC) ==Remedies== ''Note: All remedies that refer to a period of time, for example to a ban of X months or a revert parole of Y months, are to run concurrently unless otherwise stated.'' ===Glkanter banned === 1.2) Glkanter is banned from Wikipedia for one year, and is further subject to an indefinite topic ban on subjects related to the Monty Hall Problem. :''Passed 10 to 2 at 00:34, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Nijdam topic banned === 2.1) Nijdam is topic banned from the subject of the Monty Hall problem for a period of one year. This includes not just the article and talkpage, but anywhere within the project where the Monty Hall problem is being discussed. :''Passed 11 to 0 at 00:34, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Rick Block restricted=== 3) Rick Block is restricted to 1RR (one revert per day, unless reverting vandalism) on the Monty Hall article for a period of one year :''Passed 10 to 2 at 00:34, 25 March 2011 (UTC)'' ===Gill110951 reminded=== 4.3) Gill110951 is reminded to follow good practice in respect of [[WP:COI|conflict of interest]], when referencing or inserting his own sources of his own authoring into the article as references, namely to avoid [[WP:UNDUE|undue weight]], use [[WP:RS|reliable sourcing]], be able to demonstrate such if asked and to seek consensus first if editing in a contentious segment of mainspace. :''Passed 9 to 1 with 1 abstention at 00:34, 25 March 2011 (UTC) ===Discretionary sanctions=== 5) Any uninvolved administrator may place [[Wikipedia:Arbitration Committee/Discretionary sanctions|standard discretionary sanctions]] on accounts editing in this area, after a first warning. :''Passed 10 to 1 with 1 abstention at 00:34, 25 March 2011 (UTC) Amended to emphasize "pages" rather than "articles" 5) [[Wikipedia:Arbitration Committee/Discretionary sanctions|Standard discretionary sanctions]] are authorized for all pages related to the [[Monty Hall problem]], broadly interpreted. :''Passed 7 to 1 by [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Clarification_and_Amendment&oldid=631252824#Motion Motion], 05:32, 23 October 2014 (UTC)'' ::''Rescinded by [[Special:Permalink/636014759#Motion:_discretionary_sanctions_housekeeping|motion]], 11:22, 30 November 2014 (UTC)'' ==Enforcement== {{Arbitration standard provisions}} ==Amendments by motion== ===Discretionary sanctions rescinded (November 2014)=== Following a request to amend several prior decisions to terminate discretionary sanctions provisions that may no longer be necessary, # Remedy 14 of the [[Wikipedia:Requests_for_arbitration/Ayn_Rand#Standard_discretionary_sanctions|''Ayn Rand'' case]] is rescinded; # Remedy 5 of the [[Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Case/Monty_Hall_problem#Discretionary_sanctions|''Monty Hall problem'' case]] is rescinded; # Remedy 1 of the [[Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Case/Longevity#Discretionary_sanctions|''Longevity'' case]] is rescinded; # The discretionary sanctions authorised explicitly for the [[Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Case/Cold fusion 2|''Cold fusion 2'']] and the [[Wikipedia:Requests for arbitration/Homeopathy|''Homeopathy'']] cases are rescinded. The discretionary sanctions authorised for the [[Wikipedia:Requests_for_arbitration/Pseudoscience#Discretionary_sanctions|''Pseudoscience'']] and [[Wikipedia:Requests for arbitration/Fringe science|"Fringe science"]] cases continue to apply. Additionally, Remedy 14 of the [[Wikipedia:Requests for arbitration/Pseudoscience|Pseudoscience case]] is amended by replacing the word "articles" with the word "pages" for [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=&oldid=631252824#Motion consistency]; # Remedy 5 of the [[Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Case/Tree_shaping#Discretionary_Sanctions|''Tree shaping'' case]] is rescinded; # Remedy 10 of the [[Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Case/Gibraltar#Standard_discretionary_sanctions|''Gibraltar'' case]] is rescinded; # Nothing in this motion provides grounds for appeal of remedies or restrictions imposed while discretionary sanctions for the foregoing cases were in force. Such appeals or requests to lift or modify such sanctions may be made under the same terms as any other appeal; # In the event that disruptive editing resumes in any of these topic-areas, a request to consider reinstating discretionary sanctions in that topic-area may be made on the [[Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Clarification and Amendment|clarifications and amendments]] page. # A record of topics for which discretionary sanctions have been authorised and subsequently terminated is to be established and maintained on the [[Wikipedia:Arbitration Committee/Discretionary sanctions|discretionary sanctions main page]]. :''Passed 11 to 0 by [[Special:Permalink/636014759#Motion:_discretionary_sanctions_housekeeping|motion]], 11:22, 30 November 2014 (UTC)'' ==Log of notifications== On 3 May 2014 Arbcom established a new method of notifying for discretionary sanctions which is explained at [[WP:AC/DS#Awareness and alerts]]. All notices given prior to the May 2014 cutover date will expire on 3 May 2015. New notices are to be given using {{tl|Ds/alert}} and they expire one year after they are given. No new notices should be logged here. *{{user|Tweedledee2011}} notified [//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User_talk:Tweedledee2011&diff=prev&oldid=588724658 here] following an edit war at [[Talk:Monty Hall problem]]. [[User:EdJohnston|EdJohnston]] ([[User talk:EdJohnston|talk]]) 23:02, 1 January 2014 (UTC) ==Log of blocks, bans, and restrictions== Log any block, restriction, ban or extension under any remedy in this decision here. Minimum information includes name of administrator, date and time, what was done and the basis for doing it. *[[User:Glkanter|Glkanter]] blocked for 1 year to enforce Remedy 1.2. No edits should be made to this page except by clerks or arbitrators.''' *Any violations of the remedies passed in the case should be raised at [[Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Enforcement]]. *Specific requests for amendment or clarification about the decision should be raised at [[Wikipedia:Arbitration/Requests/Clarification and Amendment]]. *General questions can be raised at [[Wikipedia talk:Arbitration Committee]]. *Actions taken to enforce remedies authorised in the case (if applicable) are to be logged at the [[Wikipedia:Arbitration enforcement log|centralised arbitration enforcement log]].}} == Case information == === Involved parties === *{{userlinks|Mclarenfan17}}, ''filing party'' *{{userlinks|Tvx1}} ===Prior dispute resolution=== * [[Wikipedia:Administrators' noticeboard/IncidentArchive1015#Harrassment by an editor|ANI]] (now archived) * [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:No_original_research/Noticeboard&oldid=936366161 WP:NORN] == Preliminary statements == === Statement by Mclarenfan17 === For some time now, I have felt that Tvx1 has engaged in a sustained campaign of harrassing me, which has included [[WP:HOUND|wiki-hounding]]. This started some time around 2014 when he repeatedly referred my old account to ANI. This included [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Administrators%27_noticeboard/Edit_warring&diff=prev&oldid=901646868 selectively referring] editors to ANI, [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Administrators%27_noticeboard/Incidents&diff=prev&oldid=885956272 directly lobbying] to admins to have me blocked and trying to [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Administrators%27_noticeboard/Edit_warring&diff=prev&oldid=839435861 re-open ANI reports] without following proper procedure. Most of these ANI reports followed lengthy disputes over content, and with the admins taking no action, I felt that Tvx1 was trying to use ANI to punish me for disagreeing with me. In 2018, Tvx1's behaviour changed. He started editing articles related to the [[World Rally Championship]], but his edit history shows that his contributions are limited to [https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:MobileDiff/936418090 formatting articles] and taking part in [https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:MobileDiff/936105103 talk page discussions] where he only ever opposes me. However, some of his edits reveal [https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:MobileDiff/933408513 factual errors] which suggest he does not understand the subject. Tvx1 is well aware that I am proud of my work in these articles, and I believe that his actions amount to wiki-hounding as he tries to frustrate my editing. I have previously tried to resolve this at ANI, in which I proposed a mutual TBAN as a way of staying away from each other. Tvx1 [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Administrators%27_noticeboard/Incidents&diff=prev&oldid=908573122 responded] by proposing I be banned from editing a range of topics, which included topics that he did not edit. There was no reason for this, except to frustrate me. In preparing for this ANI, I approached an admin, [https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:MobileDiff/936646100 who advised me] that "Tvx1 is a problem user with an incredibly long history of blatantly lying/misrepresenting policy". :{{ping|Robert McClenon|Newyorkbrad}} I have been advised by {{u|Xeno}} that I can post an update here—there is an attempt at resolving the dispute underway at {{u|Chris.sherlock}}'s talk page. I would also like to re-state my willingness to be subject to a mutual TBAN, where both Tvx1 and I nominate a topic area that the other is then banned from editing. We have very little overlap on Wikipedia, so it would function like a ''de facto'' IBAN, where both of us are able to go our separate ways, articles become stable because they are protected from any dispute, and (to put it bluntly) we can both have our pride intact. Like I said, I'm open to it and I think it's the neatest and easiest way of resolving this. It just needs Tvx1 to be on-board. Happened to come across this case by accident so I'll leave a quickish comment. I've sometimes seen various disputes between these editors at ANI and haven't generally gotten very involved.

One time I did get involved was here [[Wikipedia:Administrators' noticeboard/IncidentArchive1027#User:Mclarenfan17]]. That case involved Mclarenfan17 but did not significantly involve Tvx1 AFAIK. My impression from that case wasn't particularly positive of Mclarenfan17. They seemed to bring up allegations about other editors (including Tvx1) but didn't really provide much evidence.

Maybe more importantly, the content or really formatting dispute seemed silly. It seemed to be between these 2 versions [//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_World_Rally_Championship&type=revision&diff=932564144&oldid=932562293] [//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_World_Rally_Championship&diff=932562293&oldid=932552969]. Whether to group the teams together or not. As I understood it, there was some consensus both for that article and historically to group the drivers under teams, and to me it made sense anyway. Mclaren17 was concerned because the structure of one team was uncertain, especially which drivers would be eligible for points. (There was also talk of a possible B team but that mostly seemed to get ignored.) Those were reasonable concerns, but as I pointed out in the talk page [[Talk:2020 World Rally Championship#Entries table]], as a reader unfamiliar with the subject, Mclaren17's preferred version did not seem to convey this uncertain. It seemed to me there were ways, like the use of footnotes which would convey the uncertainty while keeping the team grouping.

It was true that [[User:Pelmeen10]]'s preferred version seemed to suggest something which wasn't supported by the sources, I tried to resolve that here [//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_World_Rally_Championship&diff=932814312&oldid=932565209]. So I do also fault Pelmeen10 for not recognising the problem and trying to come up with a solution to that particular issue although perhaps Mclaren17's manner of approach didn't help. I also found, and this applies equally to both parties, that the whole thing was a little silly. By the time it made it to ANI it seemed likely the uncertainty would be resolved in less than a month so frankly it wasn't a big deal either way. And sure enough, it seems to be resolved now.

I do agree that Tvx1 and Mclaren17 really can't seem to get along, and I'm doubtful it's one sided. But I also get the feeling from what I've seen Mclaren17 has problems with other editors, at least Pelmeen10 and maybe others. And this is more so than Tvx1 has problems with other editors. Which while far from conclusive this is concerning.

This conflict centers around the style and formatting of articles in the area of [[motorsports]], including but not exclusive to [[rallying]] and [[Formula 1]]. :''Passed 11 to 0 at 22:43, 30 March 2020 (UTC)'' ===Conflict between Mclarenfan17 and Tvx1=== 2) There is ongoing conflict between Mclarenfan17 and Tvx1, which has continued for many years ([https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Administrators%27_noticeboard/3RRArchive242#User:Prisonermonkeys_reported_by_User:Tvx1_(Result:_)], [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2018_World_Rally_Championship], [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Administrators%27_noticeboard/Edit_warring&diff=prev&oldid=838955788&diffmode=source]). The two parties have repeatedly been the subject of attempts at dispute resolution ([https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Dispute_resolution_noticeboard/Archive_183#2020_Formula_One_World_Championship], [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Dispute_resolution_noticeboard/Archive_179#Talk:2019_World_Rally_Championship], [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Administrators%27_noticeboard/IncidentArchive1015#Harrassment_by_an_editor], [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Dispute_resolution_noticeboard/Archive_171#2019_World_Rally_Championship], [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Dispute_resolution_noticeboard/Archive_167#Wikipedia_talk:WikiProject_Formula_One#2014_and_2015_teams_and_drivers_tables], [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Dispute_resolution_noticeboard/Archive_158#Talk:2017_FIA_Formula_One_World_Championship#Order_of_Toro_Rosso_drivers]). :''Passed 11 to 0 at 22:43, 30 March 2020 (UTC)'' === Aspersions and battleground conduct by Mclarenfan17 === 3) Mclarenfan17 has cast aspersions and exhibited battleground conduct towards multiple editors, especially under his previous account Prisonermonkeys (e.g. [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=&diff=prev&oldid=846114718], [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=&diff=prev&oldid=781812326], [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=&diff=prev&oldid=693656600]). More recently, his comments have reduced in severity (e.g. [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=&diff=prev&oldid=880112422], [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=&diff=prev&oldid=928243169&diffmode=source]). :''Passed 11 to 0 at 22:43, 30 March 2020 (UTC)'' ===Previous blocks of Mclarenfan17=== 4) Mclarenfan17 has been blocked several times for edit warring, under their previous account ([https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special:Log/block&page=Prisonermonkeys block log]). :''Passed 11 to 0 at 22:43, 30 March 2020 (UTC)'' === Previous blocks of Tvx1 === 5) Tvx1 was previously blocked for wikilawyering and failure to abide by consensus ([https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special:Log&type=block&page=User:Tvx1 block log], [[w:User talk:Tvx1/Archive 5#Unblock request|unblock request]]). :''Passed 11 to 0 at 22:43, 30 March 2020 (UTC)'' ==Remedies== ''Note: All remedies that refer to a period of time, for example to a ban of X months or a revert parole of Y months, are to run concurrently unless otherwise stated.'' ===Mclarenfan17 and Tvx1 interaction ban=== 1) {{user|Mclarenfan17 }} and {{user|Tvx1}} are indefinitely prohibited from [[WP:IBAN|interacting with, or commenting on]], each other anywhere on Wikipedia (subject to the [[Wikipedia:Banning policy#Exceptions to limited bans|ordinary exceptions]]). :''Passed 11 to 0 at 22:43, 30 March 2020 (UTC)'' ==Enforcement== {{Arbitration standard provisions}} ==Enforcement log== {{Wikipedia:Arbitration Committee/Enforcement log section}} [[Category:Wikipedia arbitration cases|{{SUBPAGENAME}}]] {{NOINDEX}}

cases.title: Wikipedia:Requests for arbitration/Mr-Natural-Health
cases.content:
'''Case closed'''

Please do not edit this page directly if you are not a participant in this case. Comments are very welcome on the Talk page, and will be read, in full. Evidence, no matter who can provide it, is very welcome at [[/Evidence]]. Evidence is more useful than comments. 

==Statment of complaints ==

=== Complaint by David Gerard ===

After many running edit wars and extensive talk page discussion on
[[Talk:Alternative medicine]] and [[Talk:Iridology]], I tried asking
[[User:Mr-Natural-Health]] if we could sort this out otherwise, or at worst get it
mediated
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=User_talk:Mr-Natural-Health&diff=3761684&oldid=3759006].
He refused abusively 
([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=User_talk:Mr-Natural-Health&diff=3764139&oldid=3763580 reply and edit summary]). So, with all other avenues of
resolution refused, asking the AC if their previous attempt to moderate
MNH's posting behaviour worked is what's left. Or should I take it to
[[Wikipedia:Requests for comment]] first, if you think that would be productive?

MNH appears not to grasp [[NPOV]]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3610918&oldid=3610860]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Wikipedia:Requests_for_comment/Theresa_Knott&diff=3739221&oldid=3738539]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3608024&oldid=3607333]. He is given to combative discussion on talk
pages - he appears to see his mission as pushing one side, rather than
improving an article
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3756881&oldid=3750165]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3239913&oldid=3239900]. He seems to actually believe that those of
differing view are "trolls" [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3761990&oldid=3761798]
[[User_talk:Mr-Natural-Health#Memo_to_Myself_-_A_troll_is_a_troll%2C_even_with_the_word_science_in_front_of_it%21|talk page]] and "liars" [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3628268&oldid=3627691]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3621112&oldid=3621048]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3610730&oldid=3610428]
rather than
being people who disagree with him.

He takes questioning his edits or edit summaries and asking for explanation
as being "personal attacks"
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Iridology&diff=3748250&oldid=3748214]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3632182&oldid=3632091]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3422951&oldid=3422277]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3370243&oldid=3370228]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3367408&oldid=3364063]
but makes personal attacks on
others
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Wikipedia_talk:NPOV_dispute&diff=3632231&oldid=3632213]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Chelation_therapy&action=history]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3762887&oldid=3762445]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Iridology&diff=3691288&oldid=3691098]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3610730&oldid=3610428]
and maintains pages of personal
attacks on others on his user page ([[User:Mr-Natural-Health/2wB1g9Gq]],
[[User:Mr-Natural-Health/6pV1g8Gq]]). Even when his abusiveness is
deleted from talk pages, it's still in the edit summaries
([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Alternative_medicine&action=history
Alternative Medicine history],
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Iridology&action=history
Iridology history]). Apparently, getting into a disagreement with him
warrants comparisons to Hitler and Nazis
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Wikipedia:Requests_for_comment/Theresa_Knott&diff=3741708&oldid=3739940]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Wikipedia:Requests_for_comment/Theresa_Knott&diff=0&oldid=3757310].

He seems to believe he can take ownership of articles and enforce his views
on who should be allowed to edit them [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3673143&oldid=3673086]. He views article
editing as a battle with winners and losers
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Iridology&diff=3793210&oldid=3788265]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Iridology&diff=3794895&oldid=3794691]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3678289&oldid=3677356]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3628268&oldid=3627691]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3441614&oldid=3431643]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3351168&oldid=3340583]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3192637&oldid=3192609]. His combative attitude has already discouraged others from contributing to
articles he edits ([[Wikipedia:Requests_for_comment/Theresa_Knott#Response]]).
The analysis there is that
his behaviour represents attempted [[enclosure]] of alternative medicine
articles on Wikipedia; I am inclined to concur. He has constructed a
personal style guide for alternative medicine articles
([[Wikipedia:Wikiproject:Alternative Medicine/Standards of Quality]]), which
is far from
an objectionable idea in itself, but he represents it as enforceable Wikipedia policy
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Wikipedia_talk:Wikiproject:Alternative_Medicine/Standards_of_Quality&diff=3703985&oldid=3669755]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Iridology&diff=3691288&oldid=3691098]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3370616&oldid=3370332]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3303215&oldid=3303006]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3309451&oldid=3307864],
removes edits of others using it as
justification as if it's hard Wikipedia policy [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3604452&oldid=3604418]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3608770&oldid=3608695]
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3307748&oldid=3307710]
and removes others'
questions as to it being used like this [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3631663&oldid=3631598].

He encourages gross disrespect for Wikipedia bans on other users, offering to proxy for them
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Iridology&diff=3628508&oldid=3628347]. When asked not to do this [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=User_talk:Mr-Natural-Health&diff=3787845&oldid=3764139],
he removes the request with an
abusive edit summary [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=User_talk:Mr-Natural-Health&diff=3799778&oldid=3787845].

*As a side issue, a lot of medical article are getting a footer "See also:category alternative medicine" by Mr. Natural health.  The comment is not relevant to the articles.  It would be about as relevent as putting "See also: Category Metalworking" in all articles regarding woodworking.  When a reference is made it implies there is something specific to the article at hand in the referenced article.  That there is merely a general article is not sufficient reason to direct the readers attention to another place in Wikipedia.  Stephen Holland, M.D. [[User:Kd4ttc|Kd4ttc]] 04:26, 3 Jun 2004 (UTC)

**On further review, there are actually two problems.  The category entry on many articles of alternative medicine is just wrong.  Cholesterol is not a type of alternative medicine, for example.  The second problem is that a number of articles are being described as being part of the CAM project when those articles were never created by anyone involved in said project.  They are simply being annoted to imply that there is a group interested in an alternative medicine POV that worked to author those projects.  Where inappropriate these links should be removed.  Given the large number of misidentifications, the process should be conducted by a bot. [[User:Kd4ttc|Kd4ttc]] 21:47, 3 Jun 2004 (UTC)

<small>The following comment was deleted from the ''Response to Additional Complaint'' section below by [[User:Mr-Natural-Health|MNH]] ([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Wikipedia:Requests_for_arbitration/Mr-Natural-Health&diff=4047238&oldid=4047174]). Although it was posted in the wrong section of this page, it should be retained rather than merely deleted, though [[User:Mr-Natural-Health|MNH] comments in a later edit summary ([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Wikipedia:Requests_for_arbitration/Mr-Natural-Health&action=history]) that he will "continue to delete any comments made in my responses section by someone other than [him]".</small>

:Comment - the [[:Category:Applied CAM]] popped up one day after a I deleted a number of inappropriate categorizations that were made. Category [[:Category:Applied CAM]] then popped up. The request to M-NH was to stop adding the category, not create a new category. Additionally, the discussion about why the category was not appropriate pointed out that for his purposes, creating a list of related articles was appropriate. That an article with a list of CAM related articles is different from adding a category label to a bunch of articles has been a reality that Mr-NH has refused to accept. Actually, it doesn't strike me that alt med is a category of medicine, but I can see others having that view and it makes for a better medical article for having the alternate viewpoint. Thus, I can see that that link is OK because a general comment about alt med is a reasonable link in a general article about medicine. Still doesn't justify having see also alt med bringing readers to a general statement about alt med in articles like Mineral and Walking. [[User:Kd4ttc|Kd4ttc]] 00:11, 12 Jun 2004 (UTC)

===Additional Complaint===
A number of Wikipedia contributors have disagreed with placement of categories in a number of locations regarding alternative medicine.  Many of the categorizations as alternative medicine have not been edited.  this suggests to me that the editors of the articles are using discretion in judging if the alternative medicine categorizations is appropriate.  In the case of [[Clinical depression]] a number of individuals have disagreed with the categorization of that article as Alternative medicine.  This was discussed in the Talk page for that article.  Mr. Natural Health has posted the following appeared in [[Talk:Clinical_depression]]:
*Since '''these science people have only demonstrated bigoted, obnoxious, time wasting behavior towards this WikiProject''' they are clearly more interested in trolling then in improving Wikipedia.  Everywhere we have actually bothered to state our views, our ASBs etc. have been deleted / vandalized. Everywhere where we have wasted time doing what you people have asked for our ASBs etc. have been deleted / vandalized. Do you really think that I am going to waste my time wading through the above garbage that was written by a bunch of ignorant bigots? ::-- [[User:Mr-Natural-Health|John Gohde]] 14:29, 6 Jun 2004 (UTC)
His comment is inappropriate. [[User:Kd4ttc|Kd4ttc]] 16:03, 6 Jun 2004 (UTC)
**I find your bigoted behavior totally inappropriate. A bigot is: "One who is strongly partial to one's own group, religion, race, or politics and is intolerant of those who differ."  And, I find this bigoted, obnoxious, time wasting behavior of yours totally inappropriate. -- [[User:Mr-Natural-Health|John Gohde | [[User talk:Mr-Natural-Health|Talk]]]] 07:55, 8 Jun 2004 (UTC)
***Furthermore, you do not even have the legal standing to make this complaint. Please stop, wasting more of my time. -- [[User:Mr-Natural-Health|John Gohde | [[User talk:Mr-Natural-Health|Talk]]]] 08:51, 8 Jun 2004 (UTC)
****This is a website not a court. No one needs a legal standing to make a compliant. [[User:Theresa knott|theresa knott]] 08:55, 8 Jun 2004 (UTC)
*****Good, I want to complain about you. -- [[User:Mr-Natural-Health|John Gohde | [[User talk:Mr-Natural-Health|Talk]]]] 09:17, 8 Jun 2004 (UTC)

===Requested relief===

It's hard to put this in terms of specific actions. He knows a huge amount about the area and could possibly contribute brilliantly. What I ''really want'' is for MNH to:

*grasp the concept of NPOV, and not see his mission here as pushing a POV
*learn how to work better with others
*understand that the people disagreeing with him are not therefore liars or trolls
*assume good faith
*learn what a personal attack is or isn't and stop making them.

All of these are necessary but difficult to quantify.

Can anything reasonable be done short of asking him to
go away again? - [[User:David Gerard|David Gerard]] 09:44, 31 May 2004 (UTC)

:I think David is living in cloud cookoo land if he thinks the AC can get MNH to to stop pushing a POV and start to work cooperatively with others. All attempts so far by anyone to reason with MNH have fallen on deaf ears. A month long ban did not work. I'd like to request something much simpler. A year long ban. [[User:Theresa knott|theresa knott]] 11:46, 31 May 2004 (UTC)

::Please leave me my idealism! ''*sob*'' - [[User:David Gerard|David Gerard]] 12:05, 31 May 2004 (UTC)

::More seriously: well, yeah. A month time out made the personal attacks less voracious, but didn't affect the grasp of NPOV, add understanding of how to work with others, add understanding that people could legitimately disagree with him, add any tendency to assume good faith or add any understanding of what is and isn't a personal attack. A month didn't do it. Would a year? - [[User:David Gerard|David Gerard]] 07:42, 1 Jun 2004 (UTC)

:::Probably not, but I bet it would give Wikipedia enough time to undo MNH's damage and improve the articles substantially before the people inclined to work on these articles have to take a while off to go through the AC again. [[User:Snowspinner|Snowspinner]] 20:13, Jun 10, 2004 (UTC)

::::It would also go a long way to showing that the "constant edit wars on AM articles"  are because of his presence and not because the AM articles need special treatment or extra rules. [[User:Theresa knott|theresa knott]] 08:50, 11 Jun 2004 (UTC)

==Response by Mr-Natural-Health==
Starting at the beginning, David's request for arbitration was made on 31 May 2004 [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Wikipedia:Requests_for_arbitration&diff=3801222&oldid=3799756]. Thus, his request for arbitration was intentionally made ''after'' his attempts to goad me into more conflict and wasted time dealing with David failed [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Iridology&oldid=4036390#MNH_refusal_to_post_to_talk_pages] by 27 May 2004 .  I did in fact informed him in talk that I wished to stop editing these articles effective immediately on 25 May 2004 ([http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&diff=3728653&oldid=3726970], [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=User_talk:Mr-Natural-Health&oldid=4054196#Memo_to_Myself_-_A_troll_is_a_troll.2C_even_with_the_word_science_in_front_of_it.21],[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Alternative_medicine&diff=3730092&oldid=3728175]). My last edit to [[Iridology]] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Iridology&diff=3727955&oldid=3726828] and my last intended edit in [[alternative medicine]] [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Alternative_medicine&diff=3730092&oldid=3728175] was made prior to the commencement of David's arbitration request was made on 25 May 2004.  However, in [[alternative medicine]] a few unexpected events happened. I reverted [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Alternative_medicine&diff=3789712&oldid=3789467] a revert made against [[User:Heidimo]] by David who is  a participant of the Wikiproject on Alternative medicine (I feel that I should support the active participants of our project).  Then [[User:Geni]] tried to add links to professional wrestling on 30 May 2004, so I had to do 2 separate edits [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Alternative_medicine&diff=3790746&oldid=3790564] before Geni figured out his mistake. I also did one copy edit.  All of this unexpected editing, took place on 30 May 2004.

Thus, I submit that David's request for arbitration was in fact just another cleverly disguised attempt to goad me into more conflict and wasted time dealing with David.

It is my position that David Gerard, and his ilk, are the ones who have created the never-ending spiral of editing in [[alternative medicine]].  They are the ones constantly changing the definition of alternative medicine.  They are the ones who are constantly trying to stir up controversy and goad me into attacking them in [[Talk:Alternative medicine]].  How many times do they need to add controversy to [[alternative medicine]]?  Currently, they are trying to encourage a new editor into stirring up an issue that was resolved months ago.  This is their tactic.  They are constantly trying to bring up old issues in talk and goad me into attacking them.

David Gerard stated that: ''After many running edit wars and extensive talk page discussion on
[[Talk:Alternative medicine]] and [[Talk:Iridology]], I tried asking
[[User:Mr-Natural-Health]] if we could sort this out otherwise, or at worst get it
mediated
[http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=User_talk:Mr-Natural-Health&diff=3761684&oldid=3759006].''

The facts are that there were no edit wars in either [[Alternative medicine]] or in [[Iridology]] articles during this time period.

My edits of [[Iridology]] were relatively minor and were strictly made in regards to the objectives of [[Wikipedia:Wikiproject:Alternative Medicine|Wikiproject on Alternative Medicine]].  A section was added in order to add citations to research with a standard format which at the time was not currently being used.  It was viciously attacked and changed all around.  It, however, is still essentially a part of the article [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Iridology&oldid=3870087#References]. I, also, attempted repeatedly to clean up the introduction to this article, but eventually gave up.  I was harassed by David throughout my edits on [[Iridology]] and on talk.  I am still waiting for David to respond to a simple question of mine on talk [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Iridology&oldid=4006331#Can_you_see_my_replies_now_David.3F__I_am_still_waiting_for_a_response.21].  My experiences on [[Iridology]] were so negative with David, that I dropped the requirement of the
[[Wikipedia:Wikiproject:Alternative Medicine|Wikiproject on Alternative Medicine]] to add research citations to the [[branches of alternative medicine]] articles and to drop the standards of knowledge classifications from our infoboxes.  As I have yet to conduct a compliance audit on this article, I am unable to quantify how this article rates per our standards of quality guidelines [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Wikiproject:Alternative_Medicine/Standards_of_Quality].

Contrary to the protests of David, the project's standards of quality guidelines [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Wikiproject:Alternative_Medicine/Standards_of_Quality] do in fact comply with all NPOV requirements of Wikipedia [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Wikipedia:Wikiproject:Alternative_Medicine/Standards_of_Quality&oldid=3958010#Neutral_Point_of_View_.28NPOV.29_Guidelines].

My recent edits of [[alternative medicine]] were few in number, but were very productive [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Alternative_medicine&oldid=4001475#Some_conventional_doctors_support_CAM], [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Alternative_medicine&oldid=4001475#The_placebo_effect]. I repeatedly resisted David's attempts to add a quote to the article by Dawkins [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Alternative_medicine&oldid=4001475#Criticisms].  There were a number of threads on this in talk.  Having given up on this project, I responded by adding my own quotes [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Alternative_medicine&oldid=4001475#Some_conventional_doctors_support_CAM].  David made numerous attacks on this in talk [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&oldid=3724573#The_plural_of_anecdote_still_isn.27t_data], [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Talk:Alternative_medicine&oldid=3724573#Anecdotal_evidence_headers].  David basically carried on an edit war attacking me on talk.  He generated enough verbiage to create archive #7 in approximately 10 days of posting [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Alternative_medicine/Archive_7].  I have yet to conduct a compliance audit on this article, so I am unable to quantify how this article rates per our standards of quality guidelines [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Wikiproject:Alternative_Medicine/Standards_of_Quality]. but, overall, I have been very happy with the current layout of [[alternative medicine]] for quite some time, now.  

My recent accomplishments in [[alternative medicine]] was to reorganize the support section in terms of recommending complementary medicine over alternative medicine by dropping the bulleted lists, adding section headers and moving various paragraphs around [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Alternative_medicine&oldid=4001475#Support].  I added a couple of quotes [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Alternative_medicine&oldid=4001475#Some_conventional_doctors_support_CAM]. And, concluded after Wikipedia went down for approximately 2 days and after David stopped his viscous attacks with making a profound observation on placebo treatments [http://en.wikipedia.org/w/wiki.phtml?title=Alternative_medicine&oldid=4001475#The_placebo_effect].

I decided to stop editing these articles and posting on talk because it was totally non-productive due the tactics of David.

David Gerard, and his ilk, are trolls: plain and simple.

Trolls use attitude to intimidate those who would dare disagree with them. Trolls with very minimal effort, force others into wasting their time. A troll often expects you to do their thinking for them, for the troll is too important to use up their own time. The aim of the troll is to intimidate you into doing all the work, or better yet flaming them. There is nothing about the correct definition of troll that requires volition. As this is a correct characterization of David, it is more of a complement than a personal attack.  And, as it is factually correct it certainly is not a personal attack.  To state that it is not a complement means that David's behavior has indeed been wrong.

David is simply excessively hostile. And, David never communicates what the problem is. And, he fails to make constructive suggestions.
